literature.headline_zh: 乙型肝炎病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期乙型肝炎病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 与连续治疗相比,有限 NA 治疗可能会增加 HBsAg 消失的可能性,尽管病毒学复发和再治疗的发生率较高。研究结果表明,有限疗法可能是专家中心针对 功能性治愈 的一种选择性的、以患者为中心的策略,没有证据表明存在严重伤害。 [10.1111/jvh.70243]

总体抗 HDV 血清流行率 为 2.7% (14/526)。患病率 在不同疾病组之间没有显着差异,但抗 HDV 血清流行率 在晚期 HCC 阶段 (BCLC C-D) 中显着高于极早期至中期阶段 (BCLC 0-B)(5.3% vs 0.9%;p=0.024)。仅在一名患者中检测到 HDV RNA(占 队列研究 总数的 0.2%;抗 HDV 阳性患者的 7.1%)。 [10.5009/gnl260141]
在可获得 HBV-DNA 结果的参与者中,87% 的 HBV-DNA 检测不到。总体而言,81% 的人曾经接受过抗 HDV 检测,而在抗 HDV 阳性个体中,66% 的人接受过 HDV-RNA 检测。 [10.1097/qad.0000000000004635]
观察到的HCC发病率总体上并未显著低于预期,但在第5年观察到下降趋势,标准化的HCC发病率(SIR)为0.53(95%置信区间,0.24至1.20)。6名患者发展为HCC,其累计发病率分别为1年时2.0%、3年时5.1%和5年时6.1%。 [10.5009/gnl260219]
在非高PAGE-B评分患者中,升高的LG2m与更高的HCC风险相关(调整后风险比,4.40;95%置信区间,1.26–15.44),而AFP在单独分析中未能显著分层HCC风险。 [10.1111/jgh.70792]
literature.trend_or_risk_zh: 本期研究方向以入选文献实际覆盖的临床、流行病学、宿主生态、诊断或分子监测主题为准。
literature.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
key_findings_en: Finite NA therapy may increase the probability of HBsAg loss compared to continuous therapy, despite higher rates of virologic relapse and retreatment. The findings suggest that finite therapy could be a selective, patient-centered strategy toward functional cure in expert centers, with no evidence of severe harm. [10.1111/jvh.70243]

The overall anti-HDV seroprevalence was 2.7% (14/526). Prevalence did not differ significantly across disease groups, but anti-HDV seroprevalence was significantly higher in advanced HCC stages (BCLC C-D) than in very early-to-intermediate stages (BCLC 0-B) (5.3% vs 0.9%; p=0.024). [10.5009/gnl260141]
Up to 5 years of follow-up (117 814 person-years), we documented 635 incident cirrhosis and 164 HCC cases. [10.1136/gutjnl-2025-335449]

Among participants with available HBV-DNA result, 87% had undetectable HBV-DNA. Overall, 81% had ever undergone anti-HDV testing and, among anti-HDV-positive individuals, 66% had undergone HDV-RNA testing. [10.1097/qad.0000000000004635]

The observed HCC incidence was not significantly lower than expected overall, but a decreasing trend was noted at year 5 with a standardized incidence ratio (SIR) of 0.53 (95% confidence interval, 0.24 to 1.20). [10.5009/gnl260219]

news.headline_zh: 乙型肝炎病毒本期公共卫生新闻动态
news.lead_zh: 本期乙型肝炎病毒新闻集中呈现以下动态。
key_findings_zh: 丹麦一所大学批准了一项由 CDC 资助的非洲新生儿研究,其中只有一半的婴儿会感染乙型肝炎 疫苗。这项研究被谴责为不道德的。 [news-5df3717d0e9410cf]
该文章讨论了一项关于炎症性肠病 (IBD) 食物触发因素的研究,并提到了猫感染乙型肝炎的病例,但没有证实或报告人类中任何特定的 暴发 或与 乙型肝炎病毒 相关的事件。该内容是解释性的,并非已确认的事件。 [news-61e346407c7b8ed9]
AusperBio Therapeutics,Inc.正在AASLD The Liver Meeting® 2026上展示慢性乙型肝炎中AHB-137 治疗的长期随访数据。该数据与临床试验相关,而不是暴发或公共卫生事件。 [news-bec1572c8899768b]
巴西一项为期 14 年的分析发现,癌症患者中 乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 暴露量有所下降,但男性、老年人和非白人患者之间仍然存在差异。该研究发表在《癌症原因与控制》杂志上。 [news-c6ef7532078cd6bd]
科学家们开发了一种表观遗传沉默方法来靶向感染小鼠和猴子中的 HBV DNA,该方法有可能取代 慢性乙型肝炎(N12、N14、N15、N17)的每日 抗病毒药物 药丸。 [news-6e72dcc08ac151a1]
news.trend_or_risk_zh: 风险判断仅依据入选来源已经确认的信息，不把媒体推测升级为官方结论。
news.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following Hepatitis B virus news developments.
key_findings_en: A Danish university has approved a CDC-funded study in African newborns, in which only half of babies will receive the hepatitis B vaccine. The study has been condemned as unethical. [news-5df3717d0e9410cf]

The article discusses a study on food triggers in inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) and mentions a case of hepatitis B from a cat, but does not confirm or report any specific outbreak or event related to hepatitis B virus in humans. The content is interpretive and not a confirmed event. [news-61e346407c7b8ed9]

AusperBio Therapeutics, Inc. is presenting long-term follow-up data of AHB-137 treatment in chronic hepatitis B at AASLD The Liver Meeting® 2026. The data is related to clinical trials, not an outbreak or public health event. [news-bec1572c8899768b]

A fourteen-year analysis from Brazil found a decline in hepatitis B virus (HBV) exposure among cancer patients, though disparities persist among men, older adults, and non-White patients. The study was reported in the journal Cancer Causes & Control. [news-c6ef7532078cd6bd]

Scientists developed an epigenetic silencing approach to target HBV DNA in infected mice and monkeys, which could potentially replace daily antiviral pills for chronic hepatitis B (N12, N14, N15, N17). [news-6e72dcc08ac151a1]

papers.title: Finite Versus Indefinite Nucleos(t)ide Analogue Therapy in HBeAg ‐Negative Chronic Hepatitis B: Meta‐Analysis of Randomized Trials
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Continuous nucleos(t)ide analogue (NA) therapy for chronic hepatitis B (CHB) effectively maintains viral suppression but rarely results in functional cure. Finite NA therapy has been proposed to increase rates of HBsAg loss; however, international guidelines provide conflicting recommendations. This study compares the efficacy and safety of finite versus continuous NA therapy in HBeAg‐negative adults using randomized controlled trials. We included parallel‐group randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing nucleos(t)ide analogue (NA) cessation versus continuation in non‐cirrhotic, virally suppressed HBeAg‐negative adults. Two reviewers independently screened studies and assessed risk of bias using Cochrane RoB 2. Random‐effects Mantel–Haenszel meta‐analyses with Hartung–Knapp adjustment and Paule–Mandel estimation were used to pool risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Certainty of evidence was assessed using the GRADE approach. Four RCTs ( n = 357) met inclusion criteria. Discontinuation increased HBsAg loss vs. continuation (RR 5.02, 95% CI: 0.47–53.47; I 2 = 21.8%; low certainty), corresponding to ~53 additional losses per 1000 patients. However, finite therapy markedly increased virologic relapse (RR 23.09) and retreatment (RR 21.94) while reducing sustained off‐therapy virologic response (RR 0.46). Post‐cessation ALT flares were frequent but self‐limited or resolved with retreatment. No hepatic decompensation or serious adverse events occurred. In monitored, non‐cirrhotic adults, finite NA therapy may increase the probability of HBsAg loss despite predictable relapse and retreatment. With no evidence of severe harm, these findings support finite therapy as a selective, patient‐centered strategy toward functional cure in expert centers.

papers.title_original: Finite Versus Indefinite Nucleos(t)ide Analogue Therapy in HBeAg ‐Negative Chronic Hepatitis B: Meta‐Analysis of Randomized Trials

analysis.scope_and_question: This study investigates the efficacy and safety of finite versus continuous nucleos(t)ide analogue (NA) therapy in HBeAg-negative adults with chronic hepatitis B (CHB). The central question is whether finite therapy increases the probability of HBsAg loss while managing virologic relapse and adverse events.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The evidence base includes four parallel-group randomized controlled trials (RCTs) with a total of 357 participants. The review method involved independent screening by two reviewers and risk of bias assessment using Cochrane RoB 2. Risk ratios (RRs) were pooled using random-effects Mantel–Haenszel meta-analyses with Hartung–Knapp adjustment and Paule–Mandel estimation. Certainty of evidence was evaluated using the GRADE approach.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Finite NA therapy may increase the probability of HBsAg loss compared to continuous therapy, despite higher rates of virologic relapse and retreatment. The findings suggest that finite therapy could be a selective, patient-centered strategy toward functional cure in expert centers, with no evidence of severe harm.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The evidence for HBsAg loss is of low certainty, and the confidence intervals are wide. There is also heterogeneity in the results, with conflicting findings on the balance between HBsAg loss and relapse. The study does not address long-term outcomes or the impact of finite therapy on different HBV genotypes.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Further research is needed to clarify the long-term efficacy and safety of finite NA therapy, particularly in different HBV genotypes and populations. Clinical practice should consider the potential benefits and risks of finite therapy, especially in expert centers, and prioritize monitoring for virologic relapse and the need for retreatment.

analysis.summary_en: This meta-analysis evaluates the efficacy and safety of finite versus continuous nucleos(t)ide analogue (NA) therapy in HBeAg-negative adults with chronic hepatitis B (CHB). Four randomized controlled trials (RCTs) involving 357 participants were included. The study found that finite therapy may increase HBsAg loss, but it also leads to higher rates of virologic relapse and retreatment. The results showed a risk ratio (RR) of 5.02 for HBsAg loss with finite therapy, although the confidence interval was wide (0.47–53.47). The findings suggest that finite therapy could be a selective strategy for functional cure, but the evidence is of low certainty. No severe harm was observed, and post-cessation ALT flares were frequent but self-limiting. The study highlights the need for further research to better understand the long-term outcomes and effectiveness of finite therapy across different HBV genotypes.

analysis_en.evidence_base_and_review_method: The evidence base includes four parallel-group randomized controlled trials (RCTs) with a total of 357 participants. papers.source_body_en: ABSTRACT Continuous nucleos(t)ide analogue (NA) therapy for chronic hepatitis B (CHB) effectively maintains viral suppression but rarely results in functional cure. Finite NA therapy has been proposed to increase rates of HBsAg loss; however, international guidelines provide conflicting recommendations. This study compares the efficacy and safety of finite versus continuous NA therapy in HBeAg‐negative adults using randomized controlled trials. We included parallel‐group randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing nucleos(t)ide analogue (NA) cessation versus continuation in non‐cirrhotic, virally suppressed HBeAg‐negative adults. Two reviewers independently screened studies and assessed risk of bias using Cochrane RoB 2. Random‐effects Mantel–Haenszel meta‐analyses with Hartung–Knapp adjustment and Paule–Mandel estimation were used to pool risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Certainty of evidence was assessed using the GRADE approach. Four RCTs ( n = 357) met inclusion criteria. Discontinuation increased HBsAg loss vs. continuation (RR 5.02, 95% CI: 0.47–53.47; I 2 = 21.8%; low certainty), corresponding to ~53 additional losses per 1000 patients. However, finite therapy markedly increased virologic relapse (RR 23.09) and retreatment (RR 21.94) while reducing sustained off‐therapy virologic response (RR 0.46). Post‐cessation ALT flares were frequent but self‐limited or resolved with retreatment. No hepatic decompensation or serious adverse events occurred. In monitored, non‐cirrhotic adults, finite NA therapy may increase the probability of HBsAg loss despite predictable relapse and retreatment. With no evidence of severe harm, these findings support finite therapy as a selective, patient‐centered strategy toward functional cure in expert centers.

papers.title: EASL 2025 indications revisited: phase-specific outcomes with and without nucleos(t)ide analogue therapy in chronic hepatitis B virus infection.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: The impact of nucleos(t)ide analogues (NAs) therapy on the long-term outcomes in chronic HBV infection individuals outside 2025 European Association for the Study of the Liver (EASL) strongly recommended treatment indications remains uncertain. We aimed to assess the association between NAs therapy and the risks of cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) in Chinese chronic HBV infection individuals outside these criteria. DESIGN: We analysed data from 30 784 chronic HBV infection individuals across 12 centres in China. We categorised individuals outside 2025 EASL strongly recommended treatment criteria into four groups: (1) hepatitis B e antigen (HBeAg)-positive, high replicative (age <30, HBV DNA ≥8 log10IU/mL, normal alanine aminotransferase (ALT), no/mild fibrosis, no family history of liver cancer); (2) HBeAg-positive, impending phase transition (typically age ≥30, HBV DNA ≥6 log10IU/mL, normal ALT, no advanced fibrosis); (3) HBeAg-negative, low replicative (HBV DNA <3.3 log10IU/mL, normal ALT, no/mild fibrosis); (4) HBeAg-negative, high replicative, low-risk (HBV DNA 3.3-4.3 log10IU/mL, normal ALT, no/mild fibrosis). The primary endpoints were the incidence of cirrhosis and HCC. RESULTS: Up to 5 years of follow-up (117 814 person-years), we documented 635 incident cirrhosis and 164 HCC cases. In multivariable analyses, NA therapy significantly reduced risks of cirrhosis (HR 0.18, 95% CI 0.11 to 0.32) and HCC (HR 0.03, 95% CI 0.01 to 0.21) in Group 1, and cirrhosis (HR 0.50, 95% CI 0.41 to 0.61) and HCC (HR 0.25, 95% CI 0.16 to 0.41) in Group 2. No significant associations were observed in Groups 3 and 4. Findings were consistent in propensity score matching analyses. CONCLUSION: NAs therapy was associated with reduced risks of cirrhosis and HCC in HBeAg-positive individuals with high replicative or impending phase transition phenotypes, supporting the expansion of chronic HBV infection treatment criteria.

In multivariable analyses, NA therapy significantly reduced risks of cirrhosis (HR 0.18, 95% CI 0.11 to 0.32) and HCC (HR 0.03, 95% CI 0.01 to 0.21) in Group 1, and cirrhosis (HR 0.50, 95% CI 0.41 to 0.61) and HCC (HR 0.25, 95% CI 0.16 to 0.41) in Group 2. papers.title_zh: 重新审视 EASL 2025 适应症:慢性乙型肝炎 病毒感染中使用和不使用核苷(酸)类似物治疗的阶段特定结果。
papers.source_body_en: OBJECTIVE: The impact of nucleos(t)ide analogues (NAs) therapy on the long-term outcomes in chronic HBV infection individuals outside 2025 European Association for the Study of the Liver (EASL) strongly recommended treatment indications remains uncertain. We aimed to assess the association between NAs therapy and the risks of cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) in Chinese chronic HBV infection individuals outside these criteria. DESIGN: We analysed data from 30 784 chronic HBV infection individuals across 12 centres in China. We categorised individuals outside 2025 EASL strongly recommended treatment criteria into four groups: (1) hepatitis B e antigen (HBeAg)-positive, high replicative (age <30, HBV DNA ≥8 log10IU/mL, normal alanine aminotransferase (ALT), no/mild fibrosis, no family history of liver cancer); (2) HBeAg-positive, impending phase transition (typically age ≥30, HBV DNA ≥6 log10IU/mL, normal ALT, no advanced fibrosis); (3) HBeAg-negative, low replicative (HBV DNA <3.3 log10IU/mL, normal ALT, no/mild fibrosis); (4) HBeAg-negative, high replicative, low-risk (HBV DNA 3.3-4.3 log10IU/mL, normal ALT, no/mild fibrosis). The primary endpoints were the incidence of cirrhosis and HCC. RESULTS: Up to 5 years of follow-up (117 814 person-years), we documented 635 incident cirrhosis and 164 HCC cases. In multivariable analyses, NA therapy significantly reduced risks of cirrhosis (HR 0.18, 95% CI 0.11 to 0.32) and HCC (HR 0.03, 95% CI 0.01 to 0.21) in Group 1, and cirrhosis (HR 0.50, 95% CI 0.41 to 0.61) and HCC (HR 0.25, 95% CI 0.16 to 0.41) in Group 2. No significant associations were observed in Groups 3 and 4. Findings were consistent in propensity score matching analyses. CONCLUSION: NAs therapy was associated with reduced risks of cirrhosis and HCC in HBeAg-positive individuals with high replicative or impending phase transition phenotypes, supporting the expansion of chronic HBV infection treatment criteria.

analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: NAs 治疗与具有高复制或即将发生相变表型的 HBeAg 阳性个体发生肝硬化和 HCC 的风险降低相关,支持慢性 HBV 感染 治疗 标准的扩展。

papers.title: Insulin Resistance and Hepatocellular Carcinoma Development in Chronic Hepatitis B Patients Under Antiviral Therapy.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a significant concern in patients with liver cirrhosis due to chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection, even among those who achieve a virological response with antiviral therapy. This study aimed to evaluate whether insulin resistance (IR), assessed using the Homeostatic Model Assessment 2 for Insulin Resistance (HOMA2-IR) index, can serve as a surrogate marker for stratifying HCC risk in this population. METHODS: In this multicenter prospective cohort study, 334 patients with HBV-related cirrhosis who achieved virological response to nucleos(t)ide analogue therapy were enrolled. The primary outcome was the incidence of HCC during follow-up. Baseline HOMA2-IR was calculated using serum C-peptide and fasting glucose levels. RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 7.45 years (range, 0.5-8.9 years), 62 patients (18.6%) developed HCC. In a fully adjusted Cox proportional hazards model, each unit increase in HOMA2-IR was associated with a higher risk of HCC (hazard ratio [HR], 1.53; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.16-2.04). Patients with HOMA2-IR ≥ 2.3 had a significantly higher 5-year cumulative incidence of HCC compared to those with HOMA2-IR < 2.3 (30.6% vs. 12.3%; adjusted HR, 2.62; 95% CI, 1.40-4.91). The association between HOMA2-IR and HCC risk was consistent across subgroups, including those with and without metabolic comorbidities such as obesity, diabetes, hypertension, or dyslipidemia. CONCLUSION: IR, as measured by HOMA2-IR, independently predicted HCC development in cirrhotic patients with chronic HBV infection. HOMA2-IR may serve as a useful surrogate marker for identifying high-risk individuals. Intervention trials are warranted to determine whether reducing HOMA2-IR can lower HCC risk in this population.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究旨在评估使用胰岛素抵抗稳态模型评估 2 (HOMA2-IR) 指数评估的胰岛素抵抗 (IR) 是否可以作为该人群中 HCC 风险分层的替代标记。
elements_zh.methods: 在这项多中心前瞻性 队列研究 研究中,纳入了 334 名对核苷(酸)类似物治疗取得病毒学应答的 HBV 相关肝硬化患者。主要结局是随访期间 HCC 的 发病率。使用血清 C 肽和空腹血糖水平计算基线 HOMA2-IR。
elements_zh.main_results: 中位随访时间为7.45年(范围0.5-8.9年),62例患者(18.6%)发展为HCC。在完全调整的Cox比例风险模型中,HOMA2-IR每增加1个单位,与HCC风险增加有关(风险比[HR]为1.53;95%置信区间[CI]为1.16-2.04)。与HOMA2-IR < 2.3的患者相比,HOMA2-IR ≥ 2.3的患者HCC的5年累积发病率显著更高(30.6% vs. 12.3%;调整后HR为2.62;95% CI为1.40-4.91)。

elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: HOMA2-IR 可作为识别高危个体的有用替代标记。有必要进行干预试验来确定降低 HOMA2-IR 是否可以降低该人群的 HCC 风险。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 所提供的证据并未报告该研究的局限性。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 肝细胞癌 (HCC) 仍然是 慢性乙型肝炎 病毒 (HBV) 感染导致的肝硬化患者的一个重要问题,即使是那些通过 慢性乙型肝炎 治疗获得病毒学应答的患者也是如此。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究旨在评估使用胰岛素抵抗稳态模型评估 2 (HOMA2-IR) 指数评估的胰岛素抵抗 (IR) 是否可以作为该人群中 HCC 风险分层的替代标记。
analysis_zh.methods: 在这项多中心前瞻性 队列研究 研究中,纳入了 334 名对核苷(酸)类似物治疗取得病毒学应答的 HBV 相关肝硬化患者。主要结局是随访期间 HCC 的 发病率。使用血清 C 肽和空腹血糖水平计算基线 HOMA2-IR。
analysis_zh.main_results: 中位随访时间为7.45年(范围0.5-8.9年),62例患者(18.6%)发展为HCC。在完全调整的Cox比例风险模型中,HOMA2-IR每增加1个单位,与HCC风险增加有关(风险比[HR]为1.53;95%置信区间[CI]为1.16-2.04)。与HOMA2-IR < 2.3的患者相比,HOMA2-IR ≥ 2.3的患者HCC的5年累积发病率显著更高(30.6% vs. 12.3%;调整后HR为2.62;95% CI为1.40-4.91)。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: HOMA2-IR 测量的 IR 可独立预测慢性 HBV 感染的肝硬化患者的 HCC 发展。HOMA2-IR 与 HCC 风险之间的关联在各个亚组中是一致的,包括那些患有或不患有肥胖、糖尿病、高血压或血脂异常等代谢合并症的亚组。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: HOMA2-IR 可作为识别高危个体的有用替代标记。有必要进行干预试验来确定降低 HOMA2-IR 是否可以降低该人群的 HCC 风险。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 所提供的证据并未报告该研究的局限性。

papers.title: Seroprevalence and Clinical Characteristics of Hepatitis D Virus Infection in Korean Patients with Chronic Hepatitis B, Liver Cirrhosis, and Hepatocellular Carcinoma
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND/AIMS: Hepatitis delta virus (HDV) coinfection exacerbates clinical outcomes in chronic hepatitis B (CHB) patients. With emerging HDV-targeted therapeutics, accurate prevalence and clinical impact data are essential. In this study, the seroprevalence, clinical significance, and molecular characteristics of HDV were assessed in South Korean patients across the spectrum of liver disease. METHODS: This two-center retrospective study included 526 patients with CHB: non-cirrhotic CHB (n=100), cirrhotic CHB (liver cirrhosis, n=100), and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC; n=326). Serum samples (2012 to 2024) were analyzed for anti-HDV antibodies and HDV RNA using commercial assays and quantitative reverse-transcription polymerase chain reaction, followed by full-length genomic sequencing. RESULTS: The median patient age was 58.0 years, and 71.3% of the patients were male. The overall anti-HDV seroprevalence was 2.7% (14/526). Prevalence did not differ significantly across disease groups: 2.0% in non-cirrhotic CHB, 4.0% in cirrhotic CHB, and 2.5% in HCC (p=0.733). Notably, in HCC patients, anti-HDV seroprevalence was significantly higher in advanced stages (Barcelona Clinic Liver Cancer [BCLC] C-D) than in very early-to-intermediate stages (BCLC 0-B) (5.3% vs 0.9%; p=0.024). HDV RNA was detected in only one patient (0.2% of the total cohort; 7.1% of anti-HDV-positive patients). Phylogenetic analysis characterized the first full-length HDV genotype 1 genome in South Korea, which clustered with East Asian strains. CONCLUSIONS: Anti-HDV seroprevalence in Korean CHB patients is 2.7%, whereas viremic prevalence is 0.2%. Anti-HDV positivity is linked to male sex and advanced HCC stage. These findings emphasize the need for HDV screening in patients with advanced liver disease.

papers.abstract_original: BACKGROUND/AIMS: Hepatitis delta virus (HDV) coinfection exacerbates clinical outcomes in chronic hepatitis B (CHB) patients. With emerging HDV-targeted therapeutics, accurate prevalence and clinical impact data are essential. In this study, the seroprevalence, clinical significance, and molecular characteristics of HDV were assessed in South Korean patients across the spectrum of liver disease. METHODS: This two-center retrospective study included 526 patients with CHB: non-cirrhotic CHB (n=100), cirrhotic CHB (liver cirrhosis, n=100), and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC; n=326). Serum samples (2012 to 2024) were analyzed for anti-HDV antibodies and HDV RNA using commercial assays and quantitative reverse-transcription polymerase chain reaction, followed by full-length genomic sequencing. RESULTS: The median patient age was 58.0 years, and 71.3% of the patients were male. The overall anti-HDV seroprevalence was 2.7% (14/526). Prevalence did not differ significantly across disease groups: 2.0% in non-cirrhotic CHB, 4.0% in cirrhotic CHB, and 2.5% in HCC (p=0.733). Notably, in HCC patients, anti-HDV seroprevalence was significantly higher in advanced stages (Barcelona Clinic Liver Cancer [BCLC] C-D) than in very early-to-intermediate stages (BCLC 0-B) (5.3% vs 0.9%; p=0.024). HDV RNA was detected in only one patient (0.2% of the total cohort; 7.1% of anti-HDV-positive patients). Phylogenetic analysis characterized the first full-length HDV genotype 1 genome in South Korea, which clustered with East Asian strains. CONCLUSIONS: Anti-HDV seroprevalence in Korean CHB patients is 2.7%, whereas viremic prevalence is 0.2%. Anti-HDV positivity is linked to male sex and advanced HCC stage. These findings emphasize the need for HDV screening in patients with advanced liver disease.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在评估韩国 慢性乙型肝炎 (CHB)、肝硬化和肝细胞癌 (HCC) 患者中丁型肝炎病毒 (HDV) 的 血清流行率 和临床意义,为新兴 HDV 靶向治疗的使用提供信息。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项两中心回顾性研究纳入了 526 名 CHB 患者,分为非肝硬化 CHB (n=100)、肝硬化 CHB (n=100) 和 HCC (n=326)。使用商业化验和定量逆转录聚合酶链反应对 2012 年至 2024 年的血清样本进行抗 HDV 抗体和 HDV RNA 分析。
elements_zh.methods: 使用商业化验和定量逆转录聚合酶链反应分析血清样本中的抗 HDV 抗体和 HDV RNA,然后进行全长基因组测序。
elements_zh.main_results: 总体抗 HDV 血清流行率 为 2.7% (14/526)。患病率 在不同疾病组之间没有显着差异,但抗 HDV 血清流行率 在晚期 HCC 阶段 (BCLC C-D) 中显着高于极早期至中期阶段 (BCLC 0-B)(5.3% vs 0.9%;p=0.024)。仅在一名患者中检测到 HDV RNA(占 队列研究 总数的 0.2%;抗 HDV 阳性患者的 7.1%)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 韩国 CHB 患者中抗 HDV 血清流行率 为 2.7%,而病毒血症 患病率 为 0.2%。抗 HDV 阳性与男性和晚期 HCC 分期有关,这强调了晚期肝病患者进行 HDV 筛查的必要性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现强调了 HDV 筛查对于晚期肝病患者(尤其是 HCC 患者)的重要性,并支持 HDV 靶向疗法的开发。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其回顾性设计和样本量小而受到限制,这可能会影响研究结果的普遍性。HDV的总体血清流行率较低,病毒血症患病率甚至更低,这可能限制了结果的临床意义。

papers.abstract_zh: 背景/目的:丁型肝炎病毒 (HDV) 合并感染会加剧 慢性乙型肝炎 (CHB) 患者的临床结果。随着针对 HDV 的新兴疗法的出现,准确的 患病率 和临床影响数据至关重要。在这项研究中,对韩国各种肝病患者的 HDV 血清流行率、临床意义和分子特征进行了评估。方法:这项两中心回顾性研究纳入了 526 名 CHB 患者:非肝硬化 CHB (n=100)、肝硬化 CHB(肝硬化,n=100)和肝细胞癌 (HCC;n=326)。使用商业化验和定量逆转录聚合酶链反应分析血清样本(2012 年至 2024 年)的抗丁型肝炎病毒抗体和丁型肝炎病毒 RNA,然后进行全长基因组测序。结果:患者中位年龄为 58.0 岁,71.3% 的患者为男性。总体抗 HDV 血清流行率 为 2.7% (14/526)。患病率 在不同疾病组中没有显着差异:非肝硬化 CHB 中为 2.0%,肝硬化 CHB 中为 4.0%,HCC 中为 2.5% (p=0.733)。值得注意的是,在 HCC 患者中,晚期阶段(巴塞罗那临床肝癌 [BCLC] C-D)的抗 HDV 血清流行率 显着高于极早期至中期阶段 (BCLC 0-B)(5.3% vs 0.9%;p=0.024)。仅在一名患者中检测到 HDV RNA(占 队列研究 总数的 0.2%;抗 HDV 阳性患者的 7.1%)。系统发育分析对韩国第一个全长 HDV 基因型 1 基因组 进行了表征,该病毒株与东亚毒株聚类。结论:韩国 CHB 患者中抗 HDV 血清流行率 为 2.7%,而病毒血症 患病率 为 0.2%。抗 HDV 阳性与男性和晚期 HCC 阶段有关。这些发现强调了对晚期肝病患者进行丁型肝炎病毒筛查的必要性。

papers.title: Association of Hepatitis B and Hepatitis C Virus Infections With Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A Systematic Review of Virological, Histopathological, and Molecular Evidence
papers.abstract: Chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis C virus (HCV) infections are major but biologically distinct causes of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC).This systematic review synthesized virological, histopathological, genomic, and molecular evidence linking HBV and HCV infections with HCC and compared their dominant pathways of hepatocarcinogenesis.The review was conducted in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020 guidelines.PubMed/MEDLINE was searched from inception through June 30, 2026, supplemented by backward citation searching.Human primary studies evaluating HBV-or HCV-associated HCC using virological, histopathological, genomic, epigenetic, or molecular outcomes were eligible.Of 310 records identified, 278 were screened after duplicate removal, 60 full-text reports were assessed, and 25 studies were included in the qualitative synthesis.Meta-analysis was not undertaken because of substantial clinical and methodological heterogeneity.Prospective HBV studies demonstrated strong virological risk gradients.Combined hepatitis B surface antigen and hepatitis B e antigen positivity was associated with an adjusted relative risk of 60.2 (95% confidence interval: 35.5-102.1)for HCC, while HCC incidence increased from 108 to 1,152 per 100,000 person-years across increasing HBV DNA categories.Molecular studies consistently demonstrated enrichment of HBV DNA integration in tumor tissue, with recurrent involvement of telomerase reverse transcriptase and other cancer-associated loci, together with insertional mutagenesis and structural genomic alterations.In HCV infection, cumulative HCC risk increased from 1.1% among HCV RNA-negative individuals to 6.4% and 14.7% among low-and high-viremia groups, respectively.HCV-associated HCC was more closely linked to chronic necroinflammation, oxidative injury, fibrosis, cirrhosis, viral proteinmediated signaling, and persistent epigenetic alterations rather than viral genome integration.Histopathological evidence generally demonstrated greater background necroinflammation and cirrhosis in HCV-associated HCC, whereas HBV-associated HCC could occur in less fibrotic or noncirrhotic liver.HBV and HCV therefore converge on hepatocarcinogenesis through chronic liver injury but differ in their dominant mechanisms.HBV has a prominent direct oncogenic component involving viral DNA integration and genomic instability, whereas HCV-associated HCC is predominantly driven by inflammation-, fibrosis-, and cirrhosis-associated carcinogenesis with additional molecular and epigenetic effects.Viral suppression or eradication reduces but does not completely eliminate HCC risk after advanced hepatic or persistent molecular injury has developed.

analysis.scope_and_question: Chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis C virus (HCV) infections are major but biologically distinct causes of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). This systematic review synthesized virological, histopathological, genomic, and molecular evidence linking HBV and HCV infections with HCC and compared their dominant pathways of hepatocarcinogenesis.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review was conducted in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020 guidelines. PubMed/MEDLINE was searched from inception through June 30, 2026, supplemented by backward citation searching. Human primary studies evaluating HBV-or HCV-associated HCC using virological, histopathological, genomic, epigenetic, or molecular outcomes were eligible. Of 310 records identified, 278 were screened after duplicate removal, 60 full-text reports were assessed, and 25 studies were included in the qualitative synthesis. Meta-analysis was not undertaken because of substantial clinical and methodological heterogeneity.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Prospective HBV studies demonstrated strong virological risk gradients. Combined hepatitis B surface antigen and hepatitis B e antigen positivity was associated with an adjusted relative risk of 60.2 (95% confidence interval: 35.5-102.1) for HCC, while HCC incidence increased from 108 to 1,152 per 100,000 person-years across increasing HBV DNA categories. Molecular studies consistently demonstrated enrichment of HBV DNA integration in tumor tissue, with recurrent involvement of telomerase reverse transcriptase and other cancer-associated loci, together with insertional mutagenesis and structural genomic alterations. HBV and HCV therefore converge on hepatocarcinogenesis through chronic liver injury but differ in their dominant mechanisms.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review did not report on the specific mechanisms of HCV-associated HCC beyond chronic necroinflammation, oxidative injury, fibrosis, cirrhosis, viral protein-mediated signaling, and persistent epigenetic alterations. Histopathological evidence generally demonstrated greater background necroinflammation and cirrhosis in HCV-associated HCC, whereas HBV-associated HCC could occur in less fibrotic or noncirrhotic liver. Viral suppression or eradication reduces but does not completely eliminate HCC risk after advanced hepatic or persistent molecular injury has developed.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review did not report on specific research or practice implications beyond the findings on HCC risk and mechanisms.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review examines the association between hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis C virus (HCV) infections with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). It highlights that HBV and HCV are biologically distinct causes of HCC, with HBV showing a direct oncogenic role through DNA integration and genomic instability, while HCV is more closely linked to inflammation, fibrosis, and cirrhosis. The review found that combined HBV surface and e antigen positivity significantly increases HCC risk, and molecular studies showed HBV DNA integration in tumor tissue. HCV-related HCC risk was associated with viremia levels, with higher risks in low- and high-viremia groups. The review emphasizes that viral suppression reduces HCC risk but does not eliminate it entirely, especially after advanced liver injury. The findings underscore the need for targeted interventions and further research into the molecular mechanisms of HBV and HCV in HCC development.

elements_en.scope_and_question: Chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis C virus (HCV) infections are major but biologically distinct causes of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). This systematic review synthesized virological, histopathological, genomic, and molecular evidence linking HBV and HCV infections with HCC and compared their dominant pathways of hepatocarcinogenesis.
elements_en.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review was conducted in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020 guidelines. PubMed/MEDLINE was searched from inception through June 30, 2026, supplemented by backward citation searching. Human primary studies evaluating HBV-or HCV-associated HCC using virological, histopathological, genomic, epigenetic, or molecular outcomes were eligible. Of 310 records identified, 278 were screened after duplicate removal, 60 full-text reports were assessed, and 25 studies were included in the qualitative synthesis. Meta-analysis was not undertaken because of substantial clinical and methodological heterogeneity.
elements_en.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Prospective HBV studies demonstrated strong virological risk gradients. Combined hepatitis B surface antigen and hepatitis B e antigen positivity was associated with an adjusted relative risk of 60.2 (95% confidence interval: 35.5-102.1) for HCC, while HCC incidence increased from 108 to 1,152 per 100,000 person-years across increasing HBV DNA categories. Molecular studies consistently demonstrated enrichment of HBV DNA integration in tumor tissue, with recurrent involvement of telomerase reverse transcriptase and other cancer-associated loci, together with insertional mutagenesis and structural genomic alterations. HBV and HCV therefore converge on hepatocarcinogenesis through chronic liver injury but differ in their dominant mechanisms.
elements_en.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review did not report on the specific mechanisms of HCV-associated HCC beyond chronic necroinflammation, oxidative injury, fibrosis, cirrhosis, viral protein-mediated signaling, and persistent epigenetic alterations. Histopathological evidence generally demonstrated greater background necroinflammation and cirrhosis in HCV-associated HCC, whereas HBV-associated HCC could occur in less fibrotic or noncirrhotic liver. Viral suppression or eradication reduces but does not completely eliminate HCC risk after advanced hepatic or persistent molecular injury has developed.
elements_en.research_and_practice_implications: The review did not report on specific research or practice implications beyond the findings on HCC risk and mechanisms.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 慢性乙型肝炎 病毒 (HBV) 和丙型肝炎病毒 (HCV) 感染是肝细胞癌 (HCC) 的主要但生物学上不同的原因。本系统综述综合了将 HBV 和 HCV 感染与 HCC 联系起来的病毒学、组织病理学、基因组和分子证据,并比较了它们的肝癌发生的主要途径。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该审查是根据 2020 年系统审查和荟萃分析指南的首选报告项目进行的。PubMed/MEDLINE 的检索时间为从开始到 2026 年 6 月 30 日,并辅以反向引文检索。使用病毒学、组织病理学、基因组、表观遗传学或分子结果评估 HBV 或 HCV 相关 HCC 的人类初步研究是合格的。在确定的 310 条记录中,筛选了 278 条重复删除后的记录,评估了 60 份全文报告,并将 25 项研究纳入定性综合。由于大量的临床和方法学异质性,未进行荟萃分析。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 前瞻性乙型肝炎研究表明存在很强的病毒学风险梯度。乙型肝炎表面抗原和乙型肝炎 e 抗原综合阳性与调整后的 HCC 相对风险为 60.2(95% 置信区间:35.5-102.1)相关,而随着 HBV DNA 类别的增加,HCC 发病率 从每 100,000 人年 108 例增加到 1,152 例。分子研究一致证明肿瘤组织中 HBV DNA 整合富集,端粒酶逆转录酶和其他癌症相关位点反复参与,以及插入突变和结构基因组改变。因此,HBV 和 HCV 通过慢性肝损伤共同导致肝癌,但其主要机制不同。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 除了慢性坏死性炎症、氧化损伤、纤维化、肝硬化、病毒蛋白介导的信号传导和持续的表观遗传改变之外,该综述没有报告 HCV 相关 HCC 的具体机制。组织病理学证据通常表明 HCV 相关 HCC 背景坏死性炎症和肝硬化较多,而 HBV 相关 HCC 可能发生在纤维化程度较低或非肝硬化的肝脏中。晚期肝脏或持续性分子损伤发生后,病毒抑制或根除可降低但不能完全消除 HCC 风险。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 除了 HCC 风险和机制的发现之外,该审查没有报告具体的研究或实践影响。

papers.abstract_zh: 慢性乙型肝炎 病毒 (HBV) 和丙型肝炎病毒 (HCV) 感染是肝细胞癌 (HCC) 的主要但生物学上不同的原因。本系统评价综合了将 HBV 和 HCV 感染与 HCC 联系起来的病毒学、组织病理学、基因组和分子证据,并比较了它们的肝癌发生的主要途径。该评价是根据 2020 年系统评价和荟萃分析的首选报告项目进行的指南。PubMed/MEDLINE 的检索时间为从开始到 2026 年 6 月 30 日,并辅以向后引文检索。使用病毒学、组织病理学、基因组、表观遗传学或分子结果评估 HBV 或 HCV 相关 HCC 的人类初步研究符合条件。在确定的 310 条记录中,在重复删除后筛选了 278 条,评估了 60 份全文报告,并在定性综合中纳入了 25 项研究。由于临床和方法学异质性很大,前瞻性 HBV 研究表明存在很强的病毒学风险梯度。乙型肝炎表面抗原和乙型肝炎 e 抗原联合阳性与调整后的 HCC 相对风险 60.2(95% 置信区间:35.5-102.1)相关,而 HCC 发病率 从每 100,000 人年 108 例增加到 1,152 例HBV DNA 类别。分子研究一致证明肿瘤组织中 HBV DNA 整合富集,端粒酶逆转录酶和其他癌症相关位点反复参与,以及插入突变和结构基因组改变。在 HCV 感染中,累积 HCC 风险从 HCV RNA 阴性个体的 1.1% 分别增加到低病毒血症组和高病毒血症组的 6.4% 和 14.7%。HCV 相关 HCC 与慢性病的关系更为密切坏死性炎症、氧化损伤、纤维化、肝硬化、病毒蛋白介导的信号传导和持续的表观遗传改变,而不是病毒 基因组 整合。组织病理学证据通常表明 HCV 相关性 HCC 中有更大的背景坏死性炎症和肝硬化,而 HBV 相关性 HCC 可能发生在纤维化程度较低或非肝硬化的肝脏中。因此,HBV 和 HCV 通过慢性肝损伤趋向于肝癌发生,但其主导作用不同HBV 具有显着的直接致癌成分,涉及病毒 DNA 整合和基因组不稳定性,而 HCV 相关 HCC 主要由炎症、纤维化和肝硬化相关致癌作用驱动,并具有额外的分子和表观遗传效应 ts. 晚期肝脏或持续性分子损伤发生后,病毒抑制或根除可降低但不能完全消除 HCC 风险。

media_mentions.content_title: Association of Hepatitis B and Hepatitis C Virus Infections With Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A Systematic Review of Virological, Histopathological, and Molecular Evidence
media_mentions.content: Abstract Chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis C virus (HCV) infections are major but biologically distinct causes of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). This systematic review synthesized virological, histopathological, genomic, and molecular evidence linking HBV and HCV infections with HCC and compared their dominant pathways of hepatocarcinogenesis. The review was conducted in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020 guidelines. PubMed/MEDLINE was searched from inception through June 30, 2026, supplemented by backward citation searching. Human primary studies evaluating HBV- or HCV-associated HCC using virological, histopathological, genomic, epigenetic, or molecular outcomes were eligible. Of 310 records identified, 278 were screened after duplicate removal, 60 full-text reports were assessed, and 25 studies were included in the qualitative synthesis. Meta-analysis was not undertaken because of substantial clinical and methodological heterogeneity. Prospective HBV studies demonstrated strong virological risk gradients. Combined hepatitis B surface antigen and hepatitis B e antigen positivity was associated with an adjusted relative risk of 60.2 (95% confidence interval: 35.5-102.1) for HCC, while HCC incidence increased from 108 to 1,152 per 100,000 person-years across increasing HBV DNA categories. Molecular studies consistently demonstrated enrichment of HBV DNA integration in tumor tissue, with recurrent involvement of telomerase reverse transcriptase and other cancer-associated loci, together with insertional mutagenesis and structural genomic alterations. In HCV infection, cumulative HCC risk increased from 1.1% among HCV RNA-negative individuals to 6.4% and 14.7% among low- and high-viremia groups, respectively. HCV-associated HCC was more closely linked to chronic necroinflammation, oxidative injury, fibrosis, cirrhosis, viral protein-mediated signaling, and persistent epigenetic alterations rather than viral genome integration. Histopathological evidence generally demonstrated greater background necroinflammation and cirrhosis in HCV-associated HCC, whereas HBV-associated HCC could occur in less fibrotic or noncirrhotic liver. HBV and HCV therefore converge on hepatocarcinogenesis through chronic liver injury but differ in their dominant mechanisms. HBV has a prominent direct oncogenic component involving viral DNA integration and genomic instability, whereas HCV-associated HCC is predominantly driven by inflammation-, fibrosis-, and cirrhosis-associated carcinogenesis with additional molecular and epigenetic effects. Viral suppression or eradication reduces but does not completely eliminate HCC risk after advanced hepatic or persistent molecular injury has developed. Introduction & Background Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is the predominant primary malignancy of the liver and accounts for most primary liver cancer cases. Its development generally reflects a multistep process involving chronic hepatocyte injury, compensatory regeneration, fibrosis, genomic damage, and clonal selection. Chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection remain major global etiologic factors for HCC, although their contributions vary geographically and their dominant pathways of malignant transformation differ [1,2]. HBV shows a strong epidemiological association with HCC. In a prospective cohort of 11,893 Taiwanese men, Yang et al. reported a marked increase in HCC risk among individuals with markers of active HBV replication. Participants positive for both hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) and hepatitis B e antigen (HBeAg) had an adjusted relative risk of 60.2 compared with individuals negative for both markers [3]. In a later cohort of 3,653 HBsAg-positive participants, Chen et al. demonstrated a clear dose-response relationship between serum HBV DNA and HCC risk, with incidence increasing from 108 to 1,152 per 100,000 person-years across viral-load categories [4]. HBV-related risk is also influenced by viral genetic variation. The T1762/A1764 basal core promoter mutation has been associated with a substantially higher risk of HCC [5]. Longitudinal data indicate that enhancer II/basal core promoter variants may be detectable years before tumor development [6], and increasing numbers of high-risk mutations involving T1653, V1753, and T1762/A1764 have been linked to progressively greater HCC risk [7]. More recent cohort data suggest that HBV DNA level remains an important determinant of HCC risk even in noncirrhotic chronic hepatitis B [8]. A notable feature of HBV-associated carcinogenesis is that it is not explained by inflammation and cirrhosis alone. HBV DNA can integrate into the host genome, creating a direct route to genomic disruption. Genome-wide studies have shown recurrent HBV integration in HCC tissue, including events involving cancer-related loci such as telomerase reverse transcriptase (TERT), KMT2B/MLL4, and CCNE1 [9]. Genomic and transcriptomic analyses have also identified integration-associated gene disruption, viral-host fusion transcripts, copy-number changes, and clonal expansion [10]. Deep-sequencing studies demonstrated recurrent TERT involvement and structural alterations involving the HBx region [11], while newer whole-genome and long-read sequencing analyses have revealed integration-associated rearrangements and oncogenic regulatory effects [12,13]. These observations support a direct contribution of HBV to hepatocarcinogenesis and help explain why HCC can arise before cirrhosis in some patients. HCV-associated carcinogenesis differs in important respects. HCV is an RNA virus and does not normally integrate into host chromosomal DNA. Its association with HCC is therefore more closely linked to persistent infection, chronic inflammation, oxidative injury, repeated hepatocyte turnover, fibrosis, and cirrhosis. In a population-based cohort of 925 anti-HCV-positive individuals, cumulative HCC risk was 1.1%, 6.4%, and 14.7% in nonviremic, low-viremic, and high-viremic groups, respectively [14]. Viral genotype may also influence risk: genotype 1b was more frequent in HCC cases than cirrhotic controls in a case-control study [15], and genotype 1b was present in 19 of 22 incident HCC cases in a prospective cirrhosis cohort [16]. Molecular effects of HCV may provide additional steps toward malignant transformation. HCV core-gene variation has been linked to advanced liver disease and HCC, and greater sequence variability has been observed in tumor compared with nontumor tissue [17,18]. These findings suggest that direct molecular effects of HCV may contribute alongside the dominant roles of chronic inflammation and fibrosis. Histopathological comparisons support these biological differences. In noncirrhotic HCC, HCV-associated background liver showed greater necroinflammatory activity than HBV-associated liver despite similar fibrosis [19]. Other clinicopathological studies reported older age and more frequent cirrhosis in HCV-associated HCC, whereas HBV-associated tumors tended to be larger and less differentiated [20]. Greater synchronous multicentricity has also been reported in HCV-related HCC, consistent with field carcinogenesis in chronically injured liver [21]. The carcinogenic effect of chronic viral hepatitis may persist after virological control. HCV clearance has been associated with persistent enhancer and chromatin changes, supporting the concept of an epigenetic scar [22]. Residual HCC risk after successful HCV eradication has also been reported, suggesting that accumulated molecular and structural liver injury may not be fully reversed [23]. Mechanistic reviews have emphasized both direct and indirect pathways in HBV-related carcinogenesis and the major roles of chronic inflammatory, oxidative, and fibrotic injury in HCV-related HCC [24,25]. However, virological markers, histopathological changes, and molecular findings are often considered separately. Integrating these evidence streams may better distinguish the dominant mechanisms of HBV and HCV carcinogenesis and clarify clinically relevant implications for surveillance after viral suppression or eradication. The aim of this systematic review was therefore to summarize available virological, histopathological, genomic, and molecular evidence concerning the association of HBV and HCV infections with HCC, with particular attention to HBV serological markers, viral load, high-risk mutations, and viral-host integration; HCV RNA and genotype; comparative histopathology; HBV/HCV coinfection and occult HBV infection; and persistent molecular or epigenetic alterations associated with hepatocarcinogenesis. Rationale This review was designed to integrate three evidence streams that are commonly reported separately: prospective virological risk associations, histopathological differences between tumor and background liver, and molecular mechanisms such as HBV integration, viral mutations, and HCV-associated epigenetic reprogramming. The integrated approach was intended to distinguish epidemiological association from biological mechanism and to relate both to clinically relevant HCC surveillance after viral suppression or eradication. Review question and objectives The review asked which virological, histopathological, and molecular findings support an association between current or previous HBV and/or HCV infection and HCC, and how the dominant HCC-promoting pathways differ between the two viruses. Accordingly, the objectives were to evaluate virological predictors of HBV-associated HCC, including HBsAg, HBeAg, HBV DNA, and viral mutations; evaluate virological predictors of HCV-associated HCC, including HCV RNA and viral genotype; compare the histopathological background and tumor characteristics of HBV- and HCV-associated HCC; synthesize evidence on HBV integration, HBx-related effects, and host-genome disruption; synthesize HCV molecular evidence, including core-gene variation and persistent epigenetic alterations; evaluate evidence relating HBV/HCV coinfection and occult HBV infection to HCC; and assess methodological quality, reporting bias, and certainty of the evidence. Review Materials and methods Study Design and Reporting This systematic review evaluated virological, histopathological, genomic, and molecular evidence linking HBV and HCV infection with HCC and was prepared in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 statement [26]. Because the eligible literature included prospective cohorts, case-control studies, clinicopathological series, genomic sequencing studies, and molecular investigations with substantially different outcomes and effect measures, a quantitative meta-analysis was not planned. This was a multi-institutional collaborative review involving authors from pathology, family medicine, pediatrics, and clinical microbiology affiliations. The collaboration involved review design, literature appraisal, interpretation of the evidence, manuscript drafting, and critical revision. Because the study synthesized previously published literature, it involved no direct patient recruitment or laboratory experimentation. Individual author roles are specified in the Author Contributions section. Eligibility Criteria Eligibility criteria were structured using the Population-Exposure-Outcome-Study Design (PEOS) framework, a framework used to formulate focused questions and eligibility criteria for reviews of exposure-related or observational evidence [27]. The population comprised human participants with current or previous HBV and/or HCV infection, as well as human HCC tumor or adjacent nontumor tissue in which HBV or HCV status was clearly characterized. HBV-related exposures included HBsAg, HBeAg, HBV DNA, viral genotype or mutation, HBV DNA integration, and other viral-genome characteristics. HCV-related exposures included HCV RNA, HCV genotype, viral sequence variation, and molecular or epigenetic alterations; studies of HBV/HCV coinfection and occult HBV infection were also eligible. Outcomes included incident HCC, HCC risk, tumor or background-liver histopathology, viral-host integration, structural genomic abnormalities, viral-sequence changes, epigenetic abnormalities, and other molecular features directly relevant to hepatocarcinogenesis. Eligible study designs included prospective and retrospective cohort studies, case-control studies, comparative histopathological studies, molecular or genomic tissue studies, and other primary human investigations available in full text through June 30, 2026. Exclusion Criteria Studies were excluded when they were reviews, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, editorials, commentaries, or letters without extractable primary data; did not report an HCC outcome or did not clearly define HBV or HCV exposure; were animal or in vitro studies without directly extractable human HCC data; examined liver tumors other than HCC without separable HCC-specific findings; lacked extractable virological, histopathological, genomic, epigenetic, or molecular outcomes; represented duplicate or substantially overlapping study populations without additional relevant information; or provided insufficient information for meaningful interpretation. Information Sources and Search Period PubMed/MEDLINE was searched through the PubMed interface from database inception to June 30, 2026. Reference lists of included studies and highly relevant background articles were also examined manually to identify additional eligible reports. Trial registries and regulatory databases were not searched because the review addressed etiological, pathological, and molecular evidence rather than therapeutic efficacy. Study authors and manufacturers were not contacted for additional records or unpublished data. Search Strategy The PubMed search combined controlled vocabulary and free-text terms for hepatocellular carcinoma, HBV/HCV infection, and virological, histopathological, genomic, and molecular mechanisms. No automatic article-type filter was applied because study eligibility was determined during screening. The complete search strategy, including the final Boolean string and search date, is provided in the Appendix. No machine-learning classifier, natural-language processing tool, automated translation system, or automated screening platform was used. Study Selection All retrieved records were screened against the predefined eligibility criteria. Title and abstract screening was followed by full-text assessment of potentially relevant reports. Screening was performed by one reviewer and was not independently duplicated. When eligibility was uncertain, the full article was reassessed against the predefined PEOS criteria before a final decision was made. No crowdsourcing or automated eligibility assessment was used, and study investigators were not contacted to resolve uncertain eligibility. Data Extraction Data were extracted manually into a structured evidence table. For each included study, the extraction captured the first author and publication year; country or study setting; study design and sample size; HBV or HCV status; serological markers, viral load, genotype, or mutations; fibrosis, cirrhosis, and necroinflammation; tumor and background-liver histopathology; HBV integration frequency and targets; viral-host fusion events and structural genomic abnormalities; HCV sequence variation and molecular features; epigenetic alterations; incident HCC or HCC risk estimates; reported relative risks, hazard ratios (HRs), odds ratios (ORs), incidence rates, or cumulative incidence; follow-up duration; and major methodological limitations. Numerical values were retained as reported in the original studies, missing values were recorded as not reported rather than estimated or imputed, and where reports appeared to involve overlapping populations, the report containing the most complete or relevant outcome data was prioritized. Risk-of-Bias and Methodological Quality Assessment Risk of bias was assessed by one reviewer. Epidemiological cohort, case-control, and analytical observational studies were evaluated using design-specific domains derived from the Joanna Briggs Institute critical appraisal framework for etiology and risk studies [28]. Molecular and genomic studies were additionally assessed using domains informed by the Quality of Genetic Studies (Q-Genie) tool [29]. Because several sequencing and tumor-genomic studies were not conventional genetic-association studies, Q-Genie domains were adapted to evaluate sample selection, assay or sequencing validity, technical error, confounding, statistical analysis, and biological interpretation rather than applying a numerical Q-Genie score. Overall judgments were categorized as low concern, some concern, or great concern and reflected the most important limitations related to sample selection, exposure or assay validity, comparator groups, confounding, outcome validity, completeness of data, and analysis. Effect Measures For etiological studies, effect estimates were extracted as reported in the original publications, including relative risks, HRs, ORs, incidence rates, cumulative incidence, and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). For molecular, genomic, and histopathological studies, proportions, frequencies, sequence findings, integration events, and comparative descriptive results were retained in their original form. Effect measures were not converted to a common scale because of substantial differences in study design and outcome definition. papers.title: Hepatic Steatosis in People With Chronic Hepatitis B in Africa: Prevalence, Correlates, and Clinical Significance.
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT To address data gaps around metabolic liver disease in Africa, within the Hepatitis B in Africa Collaborative Network (HEPSANET), we evaluated participants with chronic hepatitis B virus infection (CHB) for steatotic liver disease (SLD) using transient elastography with controlled attenuation parameter (CAP). Using multivariable logistic regression, we identified sociodemographic, anthropometric, and clinical associations with SLD (CAP ≥ 248 dB/m), and evaluated whether SLD severity was independently associated with fibrosis. Short‐term impacts of SLD on mortality were also assessed with Cox proportional hazards analysis. We also evaluated the diagnostic performance of B‐mode ultrasound for SLD, with CAP as reference. Across 6 countries and 1601 participants (age range, 12–80 years; 39.5% female; 4% with diabetes; 11% unhealthy alcohol use; median body mass index, 24.4), 421 (26.3%) had SLD; 219 (13.7%) had severe steatosis (CAP ≥ 280 dB/m). Older age, male sex, overweight and obesity, and HIV‐negative status were associated with SLD. After adjusting for age, sex, HIV status, HBV treatment, and country, severe steatosis, but not mild and moderate forms (i.e., 248–279 dB/m), was associated with a 8.4% (95%, 1.9%–14.9%) increased probability of fibrosis. Over limited follow‐up (median 2.69 years) and small number of deaths, SLD was not associated with all‐cause or liver‐related mortality. B‐mode ultrasound had low sensitivity for SLD, overall or when severe, but specificity was 95%. In conclusion, SLD was common in people with CHB in Africa and its severe form was associated with liver fibrosis. These data support screening for metabolic comorbidities as part of HBV care and treatment in Africa.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to address data gaps on metabolic liver disease in Africa by evaluating participants with chronic hepatitis B virus infection for steatotic liver disease (SLD) using transient elastography with controlled attenuation parameter (CAP). The research was conducted across six countries with 1601 participants, revealing that 26.3% had SLD, with 13.7% having severe steatosis (CAP ≥ 280 dB/m). The study found that older age, male sex, overweight and obesity, and HIV-negative status were associated with SLD. The findings are significant for understanding the clinical implications of SLD in HBV patients but are limited by the short follow-up and small number of deaths observed.

papers.title: Becoming Physically Active and Risks of Mortality and Liver-Related Events in Adults With Chronic Hepatitis B: A Nationwide Cohort Study.
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Physical activity (PA) confers several health benefits; however, whether increasing PA among physically inactive adults with chronic hepatitis B (CHB) is associated with lower risks of adverse clinical outcomes remains unclear. We used the nationwide Korean National Health Insurance database. We included 318,131 adults with CHB who were physically inactive at the initial health screening (Exam 1) and completed a subsequent screening within 4 years (Exam 2). Among them, 58,703 initiated moderate‐to‐vigorous PA (MVPA), defined as vigorous activity ≥ 20 min/day on ≥ 3 days/week or moderate activity ≥ 30 min/day on ≥ 5 days/week. The primary outcome was all‐cause mortality, and the secondary outcomes were liver‐related events (hepatic decompensation, liver transplantation, hepatocellular carcinoma [HCC]) and HCC. Multivariable Cox and Fine–Grey competing‐risk models were adjusted for demographic, clinical, and behavioural factors. During a median 7.9‐year follow‐up (IQR, 5.2–9.5), 7609 deaths occurred. MVPA initiation was associated with lower all‐cause mortality (hazard ratio [HR], 0.89; 95% CI, 0.84–0.94), a lower risk of liver‐related events (subdistribution HR [subHR], 0.94; 95% CI, 0.92–0.97), and, more modestly, of HCC (subHR, 0.95; 95% CI, 0.91–0.99) compared with those remaining inactive. The association was more pronounced in older adults, women, never smokers, non‐drinkers, and untreated participants (all p for interaction ≤ 0.03). Initiating MVPA among physically inactive adults with CHB was associated with lower risks of mortality and liver‐related outcomes. These findings provide large‐scale epidemiological evidence supporting further evaluation of PA promotion in physically inactive patients with CHB.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the association between initiating moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA) and the risks of mortality and liver-related events in adults with chronic hepatitis B (CHB). The nationwide Korean National Health Insurance database was used to identify 318,131 adults with CHB who were physically inactive at baseline and completed a follow-up screening within 4 years. Among them, 58,703 initiated MVPA, defined as vigorous activity ≥ 20 min/day on ≥ 3 days/week or moderate activity ≥ 30 min/day on ≥ 5 days/week. The main results showed that MVPA initiation was linked to lower all-cause mortality (HR, 0.89; 95% CI, 0.84–0.94), reduced risk of liver-related events (subHR, 0.94; 95% CI, 0.92–0.97), and a more modest decrease in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) risk (subHR, 0.95; 95% CI, 0.91–0.99) compared to those who remained inactive. The association was stronger in older adults, women, never smokers, non-drinkers, and untreated participants. The study used multivariable Cox and Fine–Grey competing-risk models to adjust for demographic, clinical, and behavioral factors. These findings offer large-scale epidemiological support for promoting physical activity in physically inactive CHB patients, though the study's results are based on observational data and may be subject to confounding factors.

papers.title: Further evidence of hepatitis D occurring in the absence of hepatitis B
papers.abstract: The transmission of hepatitis D virus (HDV) requires a helper virus, hepatitis B virus (HBV) being the established companion. However, recent evidence suggests that HDV and other kolmioviruses might utilize a broader range of helper viruses, raising the possibility of unidentified disease associations. We screened anti-HDV antibodies (anti-HDV) from 2121 serum/plasma specimens, representing 1996 patients, selected from samples sent for routine diagnostic testing of various infectious and autoimmune diseases to the Virology and Immunology laboratory at HUS Diagnostic Center, Helsinki, Finland in 2021 -2022. This led to detection of anti-HDV in 20/1996 (1.0%) of patients, of which 17 were negative for both HBV surface antigen (HBsAg) and HBV DNA. Of these 17 patients, 16 were negative in HDV RNA detection, and 1 patient was HDV RNA positive. The HDV RNA positive patient was confirmed to be negative for HBV core total antibody, but positive for anti-HCV antibodies and HCV RNA. This serosurvey suggests HDV infections may occur outside HBV carriers.

The HDV RNA positive patient was confirmed to be negative for HBV core total antibody, but positive for anti-HCV antibodies and HCV RNA. This serosurvey suggests HDV infections may occur outside HBV carriers.

papers.title: Realizing personalized prediction for the reversal of chronic hepatitis B-associated liver fibrosis through machine learning
papers.abstract: Although long-term antiviral therapy can reverse liver fibrosis in a considerable proportion of patients with chronic hepatitis B, treatment response differs markedly among individuals, and reliable methods for predicting who will benefit remain lacking. Conventional clinical tools such as liver stiffness measurement and the aspartate aminotransferase-to-platelet ratio index were originally dewsigned for cross-sectional staging rather than longitudinal prediction, and their ability to capture the dynamic process of fibrosis reversal is limited. In this opinion review, we discuss how machine learning (ML) may help address this unmet need. We focus on three areas where ML has shown early but encouraging results: Quantitative analysis of images using ML, integration of pathological and clinical data through multimodal models, and dynamic prediction of treatment response based on serial measurements during antiviral therapy. In our view, the greatest value of ML lies not in replacing existing assessment tools but in complementing them, particularly through the early identification of patients who are unlikely to achieve fibrosis reversal with antiviral therapy alone. However, we also caution that most current models have been developed from small, single-center retrospective cohorts, and their clinical adoption will require prospective multi-center validation, improved model interpretability, and adherence to standardized reporting frameworks.

analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that machine learning can enhance existing tools for assessing treatment response in chronic hepatitis B, offering a novel approach to personalized prediction without replacing current methods.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings suggest that machine learning could improve the precision of predicting which patients with chronic hepatitis B are likely to achieve fibrosis reversal, aiding in more tailored treatment strategies.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited by the fact that most current models are based on small, single-center retrospective cohorts, which may affect their generalizability and require further prospective validation.

papers.title_zh: 通过机器学习实现针对慢性乙型肝炎相关肝纤维化的个性化预测
papers.source_body_en: Although long-term antiviral therapy can reverse liver fibrosis in a considerable proportion of patients with chronic hepatitis B, treatment response differs markedly among individuals, and reliable methods for predicting who will benefit remain lacking. Conventional clinical tools such as liver stiffness measurement and the aspartate aminotransferase-to-platelet ratio index were originally dewsigned for cross-sectional staging rather than longitudinal prediction, and their ability to capture the dynamic process of fibrosis reversal is limited. In this opinion review, we discuss how machine learning (ML) may help address this unmet need. We focus on three areas where ML has shown early but encouraging results: Quantitative analysis of images using ML, integration of pathological and clinical data through multimodal models, and dynamic prediction of treatment response based on serial measurements during antiviral therapy. In our view, the greatest value of ML lies not in replacing existing assessment tools but in complementing them, particularly through the early identification of patients who are unlikely to achieve fibrosis reversal with antiviral therapy alone. However, we also caution that most current models have been developed from small, single-center retrospective cohorts, and their clinical adoption will require prospective multi-center validation, improved model interpretability, and adherence to standardized reporting frameworks.
papers.abstract_zh: 尽管长期抗病毒药物治疗可以逆转慢性乙型肝炎患者的肝纤维化,但个体对治疗的反应差异显著,目前仍缺乏可靠的预测方法。传统的临床工具如肝硬度测量和天门冬氨酸氨基转移酶与血小板比值指数最初设计用于横断面分期,而非纵向预测,其捕捉纤维化逆转动态过程的能力有限。在本观点综述中,我们讨论了机器学习(ML)如何帮助解决这一未满足的需求。我们重点关注了机器学习在三个方面的早期但有希望的结果:利用机器学习进行图像的定量分析、通过多模态模型整合病理和临床数据,以及基于抗病毒药物治疗期间的连续测量动态预测治疗反应。我们认为,机器学习的最大价值并不在于取代现有评估工具,而在于补充它们,特别是在早期识别那些仅通过抗病毒药物治疗难以实现纤维化逆转的患者方面。然而,我们也提醒,目前大多数模型都是基于小规模、单中心的回顾性队列研究开发的,其临床应用需要前瞻性多中心验证、提高模型的可解释性以及遵循标准化的报告框架。

papers.title: Perspectives on primary care management of chronic hepatitis B in refugees: findings from qualitative interviews with healthcare providers in Melbourne, Victoria
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: In Australia, healthcare providers face significant challenges in meeting the niche health needs of refugees. Social determinants of health, including limited health literacy and finances, complicate refugees' access to treatment for conditions, such as chronic hepatitis B (CHB). Understanding the strategies utilised by a specialised general practice for refugees can offer guidance for treating this population. The aim of this study was to explore how primary care is currently managing CHB care tailored to refugees and to identify areas for potential improvements. METHODS: Between August and December 2024, we conducted 15 semi-structured interviews with nine general practitioners, four nurses, one pharmacist and one infectious disease specialist. We used a convenience sample and snowballing; most participants worked at a refugee-focused general practice in the west of Melbourne, Victoria, Australia. All interviews were recorded and transcribed; data were analysed descriptively. RESULTS: Primary healthcare providers in our study recognised the challenges of treating refugees with CHB, including low health literacy, and the cost of providing and seeking care. However, when compared with hospital services, the benefits of primary care include community integration and location, rapport development, and the availability of interpreter services. Subsidising primary care provider training and other costs were recommended. CONCLUSIONS: Primary care may be better positioned than hospital services to treat refugees with CHB. These findings support funding and improving CHB management in primary care to meet the needs of refugees, which will lead to better health outcomes for this disadvantaged population.

All interviews were recorded and transcribed; data were analysed descriptively. RESULTS: Primary healthcare providers in our study recognised the challenges of treating refugees with CHB, including low health literacy, and the cost of providing and seeking care. However, when compared with hospital services, the benefits of primary care include community integration and location, rapport development, and the availability of interpreter services. papers.abstract_zh: 背景:在澳大利亚,医疗保健提供者在满足难民的特殊健康需求方面面临着重大挑战。健康的社会决定因素,包括有限的健康素养和财务状况,使难民获得 治疗 的条件变得复杂,例如 慢性乙型肝炎 (CHB)。了解专门针对难民的全科医疗所采用的策略可以为治疗该人群提供指导。本研究的目的是探讨初级保健目前如何管理针对难民的慢性乙型肝炎护理,并确定潜在改进的领域。方法:2024 年 8 月至 12 月期间,我们对 9 名全科医生、4 名护士、1 名药剂师和 1 名传染病专家进行了 15 次半结构化访谈。我们使用了方便样本和滚雪球的方法;大多数参与者在澳大利亚维多利亚州墨尔本西部一家以难民为中心的全科诊所工作。所有访谈均被录音并转录;对数据进行了描述性分析。结果:我们研究中的初级医疗保健提供者认识到治疗慢性乙型肝炎难民面临的挑战,包括健康素养低以及提供和寻求护理的成本。然而,与医院服务相比,初级保健的好处包括社区融合和位置、融洽关系的发展以及口译服务的可用性。建议补贴初级保健提供者的培训和其他费用。结论:初级保健可能比医院服务更适合治疗慢性乙型肝炎难民。这些发现支持资助和改善初级保健中的 CHB 管理,以满足难民的需求,这将为这一弱势群体带来更好的健康结果。

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate the efficacy of bepirovirsen compared to placebo in achieving a treatment-free functional cure in patients with chronic HBV infection.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial was conducted in patients with chronic hepatitis B virus infection who were receiving nucleos(t)ide therapy.
analysis.methods: The study involved administering bepirovirsen or placebo to participants and assessing the functional cure status at 72 weeks through virological and biochemical markers.
analysis.main_results: At 72 weeks, a higher proportion of patients in the bepirovirsen group achieved a treatment-free functional cure compared to the placebo group.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that bepirovirsen may offer a significant advantage in achieving a functional cure in chronic HBV infection when used in conjunction with nucleos(t)ide therapy.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results could inform future treatment strategies for chronic HBV infection, potentially improving long-term outcomes and reducing the need for continuous therapy.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on virological and biochemical markers, and the evidence is moderate due to the absence of long-term follow-up data.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the efficacy of bepirovirsen compared to placebo in achieving a treatment-free functional cure in patients with chronic HBV infection receiving nucleos(t)ide therapy. The randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial demonstrated that bepirovirsen significantly increased the likelihood of a functional cure at 72 weeks. The results suggest that bepirovirsen may be a valuable addition to existing treatment regimens for chronic HBV. However, the study's reliance on virological and biochemical markers limits the confidence in its findings, and the evidence is considered moderate due to the lack of long-term follow-up data. The findings have potential implications for improving treatment outcomes and reducing the need for continuous therapy in chronic HBV infection.

papers.title: Prevalence and factors associated with hepatitis B surface antibody seroprotection among healthcare workers undergoing laboratory testing at Eastgate Clinic, Windhoek, Namibia: A retrospective cross-sectional study
papers.abstract: Abstract Healthcare workers are occupationally exposed to blood and body fluids and require effective protection against hepatitis B virus infection. Evidence on hepatitis B surface antibody (anti-HBs) seroprotection among healthcare workers in Namibia remains limited. We estimated the prevalence of anti-HBs seroprotection and examined associated factors among healthcare workers tested at Eastgate Clinic in Windhoek, Namibia. We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of routinely collected anti-HBs test records from 1 January to 31 December 2025. The first chronological test per individual was included. Anti-HBs concentrations ≥10 mIU/mL were classified as seroprotective. Results outside the assay reporting range were treated as censored but remained classifiable for the binary outcome. Prevalence estimates were reported with Wilson 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Modified Poisson regression with robust standard errors was used to estimate adjusted prevalence ratios (aPRs). The register contained 304 test records representing 299 unique individuals. After excluding three individuals with missing anti-HBs results, 296 were analysed; 163 (55.1%) were female. Overall, 148 individuals were seroprotected, corresponding to a prevalence of 50.0% (95% CI 44.3–55.7%). Seroprotection was lowest among participants aged 18– 29 years (35.3%) and highest among those aged 50–59 years (71.1%). Each 10-year increase in age was associated with a higher prevalence of seroprotection after adjustment for sex (aPR 1.14, 95% CI 1.06–1.24; p=0.001), whereas sex was not independently associated with seroprotection (aPR 0.97, 95% CI 0.78–1.22; p=0.797). The age association remained consistent across sensitivity analyses. Half of the healthcare workers tested had anti-HBs concentrations below the operational seroprotection threshold. These findings support systematic vaccination verification, appropriately timed post-vaccination testing, and documented follow-up of non-protective results. The absence of vaccination history, occupational characteristics, testing indications, and additional hepatitis B serological markers limited causal and clinical interpretation.

papers.source_body_en: Abstract Healthcare workers are occupationally exposed to blood and body fluids and require effective protection against hepatitis B virus infection. Evidence on hepatitis B surface antibody (anti-HBs) seroprotection among healthcare workers in Namibia remains limited. We estimated the prevalence of anti-HBs seroprotection and examined associated factors among healthcare workers tested at Eastgate Clinic in Windhoek, Namibia. We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of routinely collected anti-HBs test records from 1 January to 31 December 2025. The first chronological test per individual was included. Anti-HBs concentrations ≥10 mIU/mL were classified as seroprotective. Results outside the assay reporting range were treated as censored but remained classifiable for the binary outcome. Prevalence estimates were reported with Wilson 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Modified Poisson regression with robust standard errors was used to estimate adjusted prevalence ratios (aPRs). The register contained 304 test records representing 299 unique individuals. After excluding three individuals with missing anti-HBs results, 296 were analysed; 163 (55.1%) were female. Overall, 148 individuals were seroprotected, corresponding to a prevalence of 50.0% (95% CI 44.3–55.7%). Seroprotection was lowest among participants aged 18– 29 years (35.3%) and highest among those aged 50–59 years (71.1%). Each 10-year increase in age was associated with a higher prevalence of seroprotection after adjustment for sex (aPR 1.14, 95% CI 1.06–1.24; p=0.001), whereas sex was not independently associated with seroprotection (aPR 0.97, 95% CI 0.78–1.22; p=0.797). The age association remained consistent across sensitivity analyses. Half of the healthcare workers tested had anti-HBs concentrations below the operational seroprotection threshold. These findings support systematic vaccination verification, appropriately timed post-vaccination testing, and documented follow-up of non-protective results. The absence of vaccination history, occupational characteristics, testing indications, and additional hepatitis B serological markers limited causal and clinical interpretation.

papers.title: Global Reappraisal of HBV and HCV Attribution in Hepatocellular Carcinoma: a systematic review and meta-analysis of 878,083 patients reveals a recent resurgence
papers.abstract: Abstract Background and Aims The contribution of chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection to hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) has changed with advances in vaccination and antiviral therapy. We aimed to quantify their global contribution and evaluate geographic and temporal variations. Methods We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis of observational studies reporting HBV or HCV infection among HCC patients. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and Cochrane databases were searched from inception to February 19, 2026. Random-effects models were used to estimate pooled proportions. Global estimates were generated by weighting country-specific estimates according to HCC incidence from GLOBOCAN 2022. Temporal trends were assessed using nonlinear meta-regression with restricted cubic splines. Results A total of 344 studies including 878,083 HCC patients were included. HBV infection was identified in 50.4% of patients and HCV infection in 25.8%. HBV was the predominant viral etiology in East Asia, Southeast Asia, and sub-Saharan Africa, whereas HCV contribution was highest in North Africa and the Middle East, Central Asia, and high-income North America. Temporal analyses showed a decline in HBV-associated HCC during earlier decades followed by an increase after approximately 2010. HCV-associated HCC demonstrated a nonlinear pattern, increasing in earlier decades and declining after a peak around 2005. HBV&HCV co-infection accounted for 4.4% of HCC cases globally. Conclusions The viral etiology of HCC is changing worldwide despite advances in hepatitis prevention and treatment. Continued identification and surveillance of individuals with chronic HBV or HCV infection remain essential for reducing the global burden of HCC.

elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 对观察性研究进行了系统回顾和荟萃分析,检索了从成立到 2026 年 2 月 19 日的 PubMed、Embase、Web of Science 和 Cochrane 数据库。使用随机效应模型来估计合并比例,并使用受限三次样条的非线性元回归来评估时间趋势。全球估计值是根据 GLOBOCAN 2022 的 HCC 发病率 对特定国家的估计值进行加权而生成的。

elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 持续识别慢性 HBV 或 HCV 感染者并进行 监测 对于减轻全球 HCC 负担仍然至关重要。研究结果表明,需要在 HBV 和 HCV 对 HCC 贡献较高的地区采取有针对性的干预措施。

analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 全球 50.4% 的 HCC 患者发现 HBV 感染,25.8% 的 HCV 感染。乙型肝炎病毒是东亚、东南亚和撒哈拉以南非洲地区的主要病毒病原,而丙型肝炎病毒在北非、中东、中亚和高收入北美地区的贡献最高。HBV 和 HCV 混合感染占全球 HCC 病例的 4.4%。尽管肝炎预防和 治疗 取得了进展,但全球范围内 HCC 的病毒病因正在发生变化。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该综述指出,HBV 相关 HCC 最近出现复苏,在前几十年有所下降,随后在 2010 年左右有所增加。HCV 相关 HCC 表现出一种非线性模式,在前几十年中有所增加,在 2005 年左右达到峰值后有所下降。证据强调了地理和时间变化,但没有提供这些变化的详细机制。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 持续识别慢性 HBV 或 HCV 感染者并进行 监测 对于减轻全球 HCC 负担仍然至关重要。研究结果表明,需要在 HBV 和 HCV 对 HCC 贡献较高的地区采取有针对性的干预措施。
