Hepatitis B update: enabling progress towards elimination. Aust Prescr 2026;49:160-7.https://doi.org/10.18773/austprescr.2026.043 Hepatitis B is a common vaccine-preventable and treatable condition. Chronic hepatitis B is often asymptomatic and can be missed if the diagnosis is not actively considered. The World Health Organization and the Australian Government have committed to eliminate hepatitis B as a public health threat by 2030. The tools required to achieve this are available: an effective vaccine, accurate blood tests for diagnosis and monitoring, effective antiviral treatments and access to ultrasound to enable early diagnosis of hepatocellular carcinoma. Risk-based testing approaches are not effective enough to enable Australia to achieve elimination targets; hence, the Fourth National Hepatitis B Strategy 2025â2030 calls for population-wide testing to identify hepatitis B status. Chronic hepatitis B is a lifelong disease that requires long-term monitoring and follow-up irrespective of the stage of disease or whether an individual is taking antiviral treatment. Most healthcare for people living with chronic hepatitis B can be provided in primary care. All medical practitioners and authorised nurse practitioners can now prescribe antiviral therapy for hepatitis B; additional accreditation is no longer required. Holistic care includes the provision of resources in a personâs preferred language, peer and cultural support workers, access to a long-term effective model of care, and appropriate monitoring. Continuity of healthcare providers is desirable and an important enabler of sustained engagement in care. One-third of the worldâs population has been exposed to hepatitis B, with an estimated 254 million people currently living with chronic hepatitis B (CHB).1 An estimated 227,000 people are living with CHB in Australia.2 The hepatitis B virus is the second most potent carcinogen after tobacco,3 increasing the risk of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) by its very presence. Therefore, unlike other causes of hepatitis, such as hepatitis C, where significant liver fibrosis or cirrhosis needs to be present before HCC risk increases, people living with CHB have an increased risk of HCC irrespective of their cirrhotic status. CHB causes inflammation of the liver that can progress to cirrhosis and HCC. One-quarter of people with untreated CHB will die from either HCC or liver failure.4 Although treatment does not cure the infection, it can prevent progression to cirrhosis and reduces the risk of HCC. In 2016, the World Health Assembly committed to the elimination of hepatitis B as a major public health threat by 2030, and an elimination strategy was developed by the World Health Organization (WHO).5 Australiaâs ongoing commitment to this elimination goal is reiterated in the Fourth National Hepatitis B Strategy 2025â2030.6 Despite having all the necessary tools to eliminate hepatitis B as a public health threat, it is estimated that in Australia, 1 in 3 of the 227,000 people living with CHB are not aware of their diagnosis and only 1 in 4 are receiving guideline-based care. In addition, only small increases in the uptake of antiviral treatment have been seen over the past decade.2 Many barriers to accessing testing, diagnosis and care exist, including (but not limited to) the asymptomatic nature of CHB, a lack of knowledge and understanding of risk factors, stigma, remoteness, the logistics of accessing care through tertiary services, English commonly not being a patientâs first language and systematic consequences of a CHB diagnosis, particularly in the immigration system. Elimination requires a paradigm shift in the care provided to people living with CHB to increase: - hepatitis B testing through population-wide universal offer of testing, treatment, enabling earlier diagnosis - primary care provision of hepatitis B testing, follow-up and long-term monitoring of those living with CHB - the number of people on treatment. Any changes in the approach to hepatitis B management need to be developed in consultation with affected individuals and communities to ensure stigma and discrimination are addressed and to minimise the personal and social impacts of hepatitis B.7 Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people in Australia are disproportionately impacted by CHB, with an overall prevalence of 3.4%, compared with 0.8% for Australia as a whole, increasing to more than 6% in some regions.8 Aboriginal people in the Northern Territory have a unique subgenotype of hepatitis B virus (HBV/C4) that has genotypic and phenotypic markers of faster progression to cirrhosis and increased risk of HCC, which further increases the urgency for early diagnosis and engagement in care. Some people born overseas are also at higher risk of CHB for many different reasons, predominantly influenced by the prevalence of CHB in the country they were born in and the availability of a hepatitis vaccine as part of the infant vaccine schedule in that country. This article aims to provide an update and guidance for healthcare professionals across Australia to play their part in the elimination of CHB. People living with CHB are often asymptomatic and may have normal liver function tests, so an active case-finding approach is needed. A simple and cheap blood test for hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg), hepatitis B surface antibody (anti-HBs) and hepatitis B core antibody (anti-HBc) is all that is required to establish hepatitis B immune status, including the need for vaccination, or for the diagnosis of CHB. Further testing is needed to diagnose and distinguish between acute and chronic infection (IgM anti-HBc) and to assess infectivity and inform decisions about treatment (hepatitis B envelope antigen [HBeAg] and hepatitis B virus [HBV] DNA). Historically, the national testing policy had a risk-based approach to diagnosis except for the universal testing recommendation for pregnant women as a part of antenatal care. High-risk groups identified for routine testing included (but were not limited to) Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people, healthcare workers and people born in high CHB-prevalence countries. However, this approach is not effective enough to meet the goal of eliminating hepatitis B by 2030 because, currently in Australia, an estimated 32.6% of people living with CHB are unaware of their diagnosis.2 Hence, the Fourth National Hepatitis B Strategy 2025â2030 recommends universal testing for all adults as a priority action to ensure all Australians know their hepatitis B status.6 There are clear recommended care pathways for hepatitis B prevention and management for all combinations of hepatitis B antigen and antibody results (Table 1). papers.title_original: Hepatitis B update: enabling progress towards elimination

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the need for improved hepatitis B management and elimination strategies, highlighting the challenges in diagnosing and treating chronic hepatitis B (CHB) in Australia.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study is a review of hepatitis B management practices in Australia, focusing on high-risk groups such as Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people, healthcare workers, and individuals born in high CHB-prevalence countries. It reports that 32.6% of people living with CHB are unaware of their diagnosis.
analysis.methods: The study uses a combination of national data, policy analysis, and program evaluations to assess current practices and barriers in hepatitis B testing, diagnosis, and treatment. It references the Fourth National Hepatitis B Strategy 2025–2030 and the Hep B PAST program as examples of interventions.
analysis.main_results: The study found that only 13% of people with CHB are on antiviral treatment, despite the availability of effective therapies. It also highlights that Aboriginal people in the Northern Territory have a unique subgenotype (HBV/C4) associated with faster progression to cirrhosis and increased risk of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that the current risk-based testing approach is insufficient for eliminating hepatitis B by 2030, and that universal testing for all adults is a necessary step. The novelty lies in the emphasis on community-specific subgenotypes and their implications for treatment urgency.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the need for universal testing and improved access to treatment for CHB, particularly in high-risk populations. They also highlight the importance of addressing social determinants and cultural factors in hepatitis B care.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on existing national data and policy documents, which may not capture real-world implementation challenges. The evidence is moderate, as it relies on observational data rather than experimental results.

analysis.summary_en: This review highlights the challenges in diagnosing and treating chronic hepatitis B (CHB) in Australia, emphasizing the need for universal testing to meet elimination goals by 2030. It reports that 32.6% of people with CHB are unaware of their diagnosis, and that Aboriginal people in the Northern Territory have a unique subgenotype (HBV/C4) linked to faster progression to cirrhosis and increased HCC risk. The study advocates for a holistic approach to care, including patient education and community engagement, and notes that the removal of specialist accreditation requirements for prescribing antiviral drugs has improved access to treatment. While the evidence is moderate, the findings underscore the importance of addressing social and cultural barriers to effective hepatitis B management.

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究解决了改进乙型肝炎管理和消除策略的需要,强调了澳大利亚诊断和治疗 慢性乙型肝炎 (CHB) 的挑战。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究回顾了澳大利亚乙型肝炎管理实践,重点关注原住民和托雷斯海峡岛民、医护人员以及出生在高 CHB-患病率 国家的个人等高风险群体。据报道,32.6% 的慢性乙型肝炎患者不知道自己的 诊断。
analysis_zh.methods: 该研究结合了国家数据、政策分析和项目评估来评估乙型肝炎检测、诊断 和 治疗 的当前实践和障碍。它引用了第四个国家乙型肝炎战略 2025-2030 和乙型肝炎 PAST 计划作为干预措施的例子。
analysis_zh.main_results: 研究发现,尽管有有效的治疗方法,但只有 13% 的慢性乙型肝炎患者接受 抗病毒药物 治疗 治疗。它还强调,北领地的原住民具有独特的亚基因型 (HBV/C4),与更快进展为肝硬化和增加患肝细胞癌 (HCC) 的风险相关。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,目前基于风险的检测方法不足以在 2030 年消除乙型肝炎,对所有成年人进行普遍检测是必要的一步。新颖之处在于强调社区特定的亚基因型及其对 治疗 紧迫性的影响。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明需要进行普遍检测并改善慢性乙型肝炎的 治疗 的可及性,特别是在高危人群中。他们还强调了在乙型肝炎护理中解决社会决定因素和文化因素的重要性。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究基于现有的国家数据和政策文件,可能无法捕捉现实世界的实施挑战。证据是温和的,因为它依赖于观察数据而不是实验结果。

papers.title: ESQUEMA DE VACUNACIÓN DEL PERSONAL SANITARIO PARA COVID-19, HEPATITIS B Y TÉTANOS DEL HOSPITAL GENERAL PEDIÁTRICO “NIÑOS DE ACOSTA ÑU” DE MARZO A ABRIL DEL 2023
papers.abstract: Introduction: Infectious diseases constitute an important risk for healthcare personnel during the performance of their professional activities. However, in many cases, these diseases can be effectively prevented through systematic and preventive vaccination. Objective: To determine the frequency of healthcare personnel vaccinated against COVID-19, hepatitis B, and tetanus at the General Pediatric Hospital “Niños de Acosta Ñu” from March to April 2023. Methodology: A descriptive, non-experimental, quantitative, cross-sectional, and prospective study was conducted. The variables analyzed were age, sex, place of residence, length of employment, professional category, compliance with the vaccination schedule, occurrence of disease, type of disease, disease severity, and perception of vaccines. Data were collected using a digital Google Forms questionnaire, subsequently entered into Microsoft Excel 2016, and statistically analyzed using SPSS, version 21. The study protocol was approved by the Ethics Committee. Results: The mean age was 33 years (±5.5). Of the total participants, 83.1% (212/255) were female. Regarding place of residence, 57.3% (146/255) were from the Central Department. The median length of employment was 5 years (1–21). Regarding COVID-19 vaccination, 45.5% had completed the vaccination schedule, whereas 55.5% had an incomplete schedule. For hepatitis B, 85.9% (219/255) had completed the vaccination schedule. Regarding tetanus vaccination, 96.5% (246/255) had completed the vaccination schedule. Overall, 83.5% of the participants reported having contracted COVID-19, while 16.5% had not contracted the disease. Conclusion: The frequency of healthcare personnel at the General Pediatric Hospital “Niños de Acosta Ñu” with a complete COVID-19 vaccination schedule was low (45.5%), whereas the frequency of complete vaccination against hepatitis B (85.9%) and tetanus (96.5%) was high.
papers.journal: Revista Ibero-Americana de Humanidades, Ciências e Educação

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 传染病对医护人员进行专业活动构成重要风险。然而,在很多情况下,通过系统性、预防性的疫苗接种,这些疾病是可以有效预防的。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 2023 年 3 月至 4 月,在“Niños de Acosta Ñu”综合儿科医院进行了一项描述性、非实验性、定量、横断面和前瞻性研究。该研究包括 255 名医护人员。
elements_zh.methods: 使用数字 Google Forms 问卷收集数据,随后输入 Microsoft Excel 2016,并使用 SPSS 21 版进行统计分析。研究方案得到了伦理委员会的批准。
elements_zh.main_results: 关于 COVID-19 疫苗接种,45.5% 已完成 疫苗接种 时间表,而 55.5% 的时间表不完整。对于乙型肝炎,85.9% (219/255) 已完成 疫苗接种 时间表。关于破伤风 疫苗接种,96.5% (246/255) 完成了 疫苗接种 时间表。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: “Niños de Acosta Ñu”综合儿科医院的医护人员使用完整的 COVID-19 疫苗接种 时间表的频率较低 (45.5%),而针对乙型肝炎 (85.9%) 和破伤风 (96.5%) 的完整 疫苗接种 时间表的频率较高。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果可为医护人员提供有针对性的 疫苗接种 计划,特别强调需要更好地遵守 COVID-19 疫苗接种 时间表。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究是描述性的、非实验性的,这限制了其建立因果关系的能力。由于横截面设计和自我报告偏差的可能性,证据是中等的。

papers.title_zh: ESQUEMA DE VACUNACIÓN DEL PERSONAL SANITARIO PARA COVID-19, HEPATITIS B Y TÉTANOS DEL HOSPITAL GENERAL PEDIÁTRICO “NIÑOS DE ACOSTA ÑU” DE MARZO A ABRIL DEL 2023
papers.source_body_en: Introduction: Infectious diseases constitute an important risk for healthcare personnel during the performance of their professional activities. However, in many cases, these diseases can be effectively prevented through systematic and preventive vaccination. Objective: To determine the frequency of healthcare personnel vaccinated against COVID-19, hepatitis B, and tetanus at the General Pediatric Hospital “Niños de Acosta Ñu” from March to April 2023. Methodology: A descriptive, non-experimental, quantitative, cross-sectional, and prospective study was conducted. The variables analyzed were age, sex, place of residence, length of employment, professional category, compliance with the vaccination schedule, occurrence of disease, type of disease, disease severity, and perception of vaccines. Data were collected using a digital Google Forms questionnaire, subsequently entered into Microsoft Excel 2016, and statistically analyzed using SPSS, version 21. The study protocol was approved by the Ethics Committee. Results: The mean age was 33 years (±5.5). Of the total participants, 83.1% (212/255) were female. Regarding place of residence, 57.3% (146/255) were from the Central Department. The median length of employment was 5 years (1–21). Regarding COVID-19 vaccination, 45.5% had completed the vaccination schedule, whereas 55.5% had an incomplete schedule. For hepatitis B, 85.9% (219/255) had completed the vaccination schedule. Regarding tetanus vaccination, 96.5% (246/255) had completed the vaccination schedule. Overall, 83.5% of the participants reported having contracted COVID-19, while 16.5% had not contracted the disease. Conclusion: The frequency of healthcare personnel at the General Pediatric Hospital “Niños de Acosta Ñu” with a complete COVID-19 vaccination schedule was low (45.5%), whereas the frequency of complete vaccination against hepatitis B (85.9%) and tetanus (96.5%) was high.

papers.title: Modeling and Analysis of SEIR Model of Hepatitis-\(B\) Virus via Fibonacci Wavelets
papers.abstract: This study aims to examine the dynamics of susceptible, exposed, infected, and recovered individuals in the context of hepatitis-\(B\) model. This is achieved by developing an efficient numerical scheme based on Fibonacci wavelets for solving the hepatitis-\(B\) model. The proposed method employs operational matrices derived from Fibonacci wavelets to convert the given system of differential equations into a system of algebraic equations, solved via the Newton-Raphson method in MATLAB. The effects of hepatocyte death and virus production rates on healthy cells, infected cells, and viral load are analyzed to capture key aspects of disease progression. Comparative analysis with ND solve and Haar wavelet methods demonstrates that the proposed method yields accurate and efficient results. The numerical findings confirm the potential of Fibonacci wavelets as a reliable computational tool for studying infectious disease dynamics.

papers.title_zh: 基于斐波那契小波的乙型肝炎病毒 SEIR 模型建模与分析
papers.source_body_en: This study aims to examine the dynamics of susceptible, exposed, infected, and recovered individuals in the context of hepatitis-\(B\) model. This is achieved by developing an efficient numerical scheme based on Fibonacci wavelets for solving the hepatitis-\(B\) model. The proposed method employs operational matrices derived from Fibonacci wavelets to convert the given system of differential equations into a system of algebraic equations, solved via the Newton-Raphson method in MATLAB. The effects of hepatocyte death and virus production rates on healthy cells, infected cells, and viral load are analyzed to capture key aspects of disease progression. Comparative analysis with ND solve and Haar wavelet methods demonstrates that the proposed method yields accurate and efficient results. The numerical findings confirm the potential of Fibonacci wavelets as a reliable computational tool for studying infectious disease dynamics.
papers.abstract_zh: 本研究旨在检查乙型肝炎模型中易感者、暴露者、感染者和康复者的动态。这是通过开发基于斐波那契小波的有效数值方案来解决肝炎-\(B\)模型来实现的。该方法采用斐波那契小波导出的运算矩阵将给定的微分方程组转换为代数方程组,并通过 MATLAB 中的牛顿-拉夫森方法求解。分析肝细胞死亡和病毒产生率对健康细胞、感染细胞和病毒载量的影响,以捕获疾病进展的关键方面。与ND求解和Haar小波方法的比较分析表明,该方法能产生准确、高效的结果。数值结果证实了斐波那契小波作为研究传染病动力学的可靠计算工具的潜力。

papers.title: Clonorchis sinensis co-infection potentiates polymorphonuclear-myeloid-derived suppressor cells expansion and metabolic reprogramming in chronic hepatitis B patients
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND Clonorchis sinensis (C. sinensis ) co-infection is known to accelerate disease progression and induce immune tolerance in patients with hepatitis B virus (HBV), particularly in regions where both infections are endemic. Metabolic reprogramming has emerged as a key driver of immunosuppression. These metabolic shifts are often orchestrated by myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs), which expand during chronic infections to promote immune tolerance. sinensis co-infection reprograms metabolism to favor MDSC-linked suppression and how this process relates to normal liver enzyme levels remains unclear. AIM To investigate whether C. sinensis co-infection induces MDSC- linked metabolic reprogramming in patients with HBV and normal liver enzyme levels. METHODS In this cross-sectional study, a total of 117 participants were enrolled and assigned to four groups: Healthy controls (n = 30), C. sinensis mono-infected participants (n = 29), HBV mono-infected participants (n = 28), and co-infected participants (n = 30). Serum cytokine profiles were measured using chemiluminescence immunoassay, amino acid metabolites using liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry, and MDSC subsets using flow cytometry. Spearman correlation and mediation analyses were performed to explore the relationships among inflammation, metabolism, and immunity. RESULTS HBV mono-infected and co-infected patients showed no statistically significant differences in liver enzyme and HBV DNA levels. However, compared with the HBV mono-infected group, the co-infected group had higher levels of the inflammatory cytokine: Interleukin-6 (IL-6) and tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), accompanied by markedly lower interferon-γ (IFN-γ) levels. Flow cytometric assay revealed that polymorphonuclear MDSCs (PMN-MDSCs) showed the greatest expansion in the co-infected group, and their proportion correlated strongly with IL-6 and TNF-α levels. Metabolically, the co-infected group had a significantly higher ornithine-to-arginine ratio. Mediation analysis suggested that PMN-MDSCs accounted for approximately 45% of the total effect of IL-6 on IFN-γ suppression. sinensis co-infection was associated with immunosuppression through IL-6/TNF-α-linked PMN-MDSC expansion and elevated ornithine-to-arginine ratio, resulting in suppressed IFN-γ production despite normal liver enzyme levels.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the impact of Clonorchis sinensis co-infection on immune and metabolic profiles in patients with HBV and normal liver enzyme levels. A cross-sectional design was used, enrolling 117 participants into four groups. Methods included cytokine profiling, amino acid metabolite analysis, and flow cytometry to assess MDSC subsets. Results showed no significant differences in liver enzymes or HBV DNA levels between HBV mono-infected and co-infected patients, but co-infected individuals had higher IL-6 and TNF-α levels and lower IFN-γ levels. Mediation analysis indicated that PMN-MDSCs accounted for 45% of the effect of IL-6 on IFN-γ suppression. The authors suggest that C. sinensis co-infection may induce immunosuppression through IL-6/TNF-α-linked PMN-MDSC expansion and metabolic shifts. The study's findings may inform future research on immune modulation in HBV co-infection scenarios, though the cross-sectional design limits causal inference. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the reliance on correlational data.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在探讨华支睾吸虫合并感染是否会在肝酶水平正常的 HBV 患者中诱导 MDSC 相关的代谢重编程。背景强调,已知中华支原体合并感染会加速乙型肝炎患者的疾病进展并诱导免疫耐受,特别是在流行地区。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项横断面研究纳入了 117 名参与者,分为四组:健康对照(n = 30)、中华支原体单一感染参与者(n = 29)、HBV 单一感染参与者(n = 28)和混合感染参与者(n = 30)。
elements_zh.methods: 使用化学发光免疫测定法测量血清细胞因子谱,使用液相色谱-串联质谱法测量氨基酸代谢物,并使用流式细胞术测量MDSC子集。流式细胞术检测显示,多形核MDSC(PMN-MDSC)在共感染组中表现出最大的扩增,并且其比例与IL-6和TNF-α水平密切相关。
elements_zh.main_results: HBV单一感染和合并感染患者的肝酶和HBV DNA水平无统计学差异。然而,共同感染组的炎症细胞因子:白细胞介素-6 (IL-6) 和肿瘤坏死因子-α (TNF-α) 水平较高,同时干扰素-γ (IFN-γ) 水平明显较低。中介分析表明,PMN-MDSC 约占 IL-6 对 IFN-γ 抑制总效应的 45%。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,中华线虫合并感染与通过 IL-6/TNF-α 连接的 PMN-MDSC 扩增和鸟氨酸与精氨酸比率升高而产生的免疫抑制有关,导致尽管肝酶水平正常,但 IFN-γ 的产生受到抑制。这一发现强调了共感染可能调节 HBV 患者 免疫应答 的新机制。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可能有助于了解合并感染 HBV 患者的免疫调节,并可能指导未来基于免疫的治疗和针对合并感染情况的 监测 策略的研究。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究是横断面的,限制了其建立因果关系的能力。证据基于相关性和中介分析,可能无法完全捕捉感染与 免疫应答 之间复杂的相互作用。信心是中等的。

Mediation analysis suggested that PMN-MDSCs accounted for approximately 45% of the total effect of IL-6 on IFN-γ suppression. sinensis co-infection was associated with immunosuppression through IL-6/TNF-α-linked PMN-MDSC expansion and elevated ornithine-to-arginine ratio, resulting in suppressed IFN-γ production despite normal liver enzyme levels.
papers.abstract_zh: 背景已知华支睾吸虫(C. sinensis)合并感染会加速乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)患者的疾病进展并诱导免疫耐受,特别是在两种感染流行的地区。代谢重编程已成为免疫抑制的关键驱动因素。这些代谢变化通常是由骨髓源性抑制细胞(MDSC)精心策划的,这些细胞在慢性感染期间会扩张以促进免疫耐受。中华丝虫合并感染会重新编程代谢以有利于 MDSC 相关的抑制,而这一过程与正常肝酶水平的关系仍不清楚。目的 探讨中华支原体合并感染是否会诱导肝酶水平正常的 HBV 患者发生 MDSC 相关的代谢重编程。方法 在这项横断面研究中,总共招募了 117 名参与者,并分为四组:健康对照(n = 30)、单一感染中华支原体的参与者(n = 29)、单一感染 HBV 的参与者(n = 28)和混合感染的参与者(n = 30)。使用化学发光免疫测定法测量血清细胞因子谱,使用液相色谱-串联质谱法测量氨基酸代谢物,并使用流式细胞术测量MDSC子集。进行 Spearman 相关性和中介分析来探讨炎症、代谢和免疫之间的关系。结果 HBV单一感染和合并感染患者的肝酶和HBV DNA水平无统计学差异。然而,与HBV单一感染组相比,合并感染组的炎症细胞因子白细胞介素6(IL-6)和肿瘤坏死因子-α(TNF-α)水平较高,同时干扰素-γ(IFN-γ)水平明显较低。流式细胞术检测显示,多形核MDSC(PMN-MDSC)在共感染组中表现出最大的扩增,并且其比例与IL-6和TNF-α水平密切相关。在代谢方面,共同感染组的鸟氨酸与精氨酸的比率显着较高。中介分析表明,PMN-MDSC 约占 IL-6 对 IFN-γ 抑制总效应的 45%。中华线虫合并感染通过 IL-6/TNF-α 连接的 PMN-MDSC 扩增和鸟氨酸与精氨酸比率升高与免疫抑制相关,导致尽管肝酶水平正常,但 IFN-γ 的产生受到抑制。

analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可能有助于了解合并感染 HBV 患者的免疫调节,并可能指导未来基于免疫的治疗和针对合并感染情况的 监测 策略的研究。

papers.title: Predictive model to identify patients requiring extended interferon therapy in chronic hepatitis B
papers.abstract: A contemporary study by Yan et al , published in the World Journal of Gastroen terology , demonstrates that baseline hepatitis B surface antigen and cirrhosis can be utilized in a prediction model to identify populations that may benefit from extended (≥ 48 weeks) interferon therapy. In this editorial, we summarize strengths of their study. First, the follow-up period was sufficiently long; second, the authors identified all major confounding factors; third, appropriate statistical methods were employed; fourth, the figures and tables are highly legible; and fifth, the training cohort exhibited stable discriminatory ability. The limitations of the study are as follows: First, the sample size in certain subgroups was too small; second, nearly all similar studies have been conducted in China, leaving readers with a limited understanding of global trends in this field; and third, the benefits of adding PEGylated interferon α-2b to nucleos(t)ide analog therapy were not addressed. Future research should investigate the promising role of combination therapies involving PEGylated interferon α-2b and nucleos(t)ide analogs, incorporate machine learning approaches, and consider the effects of concurrent nonalcoholic fatty liver disease.

papers.abstract_zh: Yan 等人发表在《世界胃肠病学杂志》上的一项当代研究表明,可以在预测模型中利用基线乙型肝炎表面抗原和肝硬化来识别可能受益于延长(≥ 48 周)干扰素治疗的人群。在这篇社论中,我们总结了他们的研究优势。第一,随访时间足够长;其次,作者确定了所有主要的混杂因素;第三,采用适当的统计方法;第四,图表清晰易读;第五,训练后的队列研究表现出稳定的判别能力。该研究的局限性如下:首先,某些亚组的样本量过小;其次,几乎所有类似的研究都是在中国进行的,导致读者对该领域的全球趋势了解有限;第三,在核苷(酸)类似物疗法中添加聚乙二醇化干扰素α-2b的好处没有得到解决。未来的研究应该调查涉及聚乙二醇化干扰素 α-2b 和核苷(酸)类似物的联合疗法的有前景的作用,结合机器学习方法,并考虑并发非酒精性脂肪肝疾病的影响。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在开发一个预测模型来识别可能受益于延长干扰素治疗的 慢性乙型肝炎 患者。这一点很重要,因为确定哪些患者需要更长的 治疗 持续时间存在挑战。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究对 慢性乙型肝炎 患者进行了回顾性分析,重点关注接受干扰素治疗的患者。随访时间足够长,训练后的队列研究表现出稳定的判别能力。
analysis_zh.methods: 作者采用了适当的统计方法并确定了所有主要的混杂因素。他们使用基线乙型肝炎表面抗原水平和肝硬化状态作为模型中的预测因子。
analysis_zh.main_results: 该研究表明,基线乙型肝炎表面抗原和肝硬化可以有效地用于预测模型中,以识别可能受益于延长干扰素治疗的患者。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将他们的发现解释为一种根据基线标志物个性化 慢性乙型肝炎 患者干扰素治疗持续时间的新方法。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以帮助识别可能需要延长干扰素治疗的患者,从而为临床决策提供信息,从而有可能改善 治疗 的结果。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究存在局限性,包括某些亚组的样本量较小以及关注中国人群,这可能会限制结果的普遍性。由于这些限制,证据的强度中等。

papers.title: A cross-sectional study of hepatitis B vaccination coverage and occupational risk exposure among health science students in a Nigerian University
papers.abstract: Abstract Introduction Despite the presence of a safe and effective vaccine for hepatitis B virus (HBV), health science students remain at significant risk for infection. This study assessed HBV vaccination coverage, awareness, and associated factors among health science students at Usmanu Danfodiyo University in Sokoto, Nigeria. Methodology A cross-sectional study targeting 427 health science students was conducted at Usmanu Danfodiyo University Sokoto between July 19 and September 10, 2025. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire assessing hepatitis B awareness, vaccination status, barriers, motivators, and occupational risks. Analysis used IBM SPSS version 25, with descriptive statistics, chi-square tests ( p < 0.05), and binary logistic regression, while the Hosmer–Lemeshow test and Nagelkerke R2 assessed model fit and explained variance. Results A total of 410 students participated (mean age 22.36 ± 2.94 years). Awareness of the hepatitis B vaccine was high (87.8%), but uptake was low (26.8%), only 12.2% were fully vaccinated, and 50.7% of unvaccinated students were willing to vaccinate. Key barriers included vaccine inaccessibility, cost, and limited information, while major motivators were prior exposure to infection (57.3%), institutional requirements (47.6%), and trust in public health institutions (43.9%). Occupational exposures were common, with poor post-exposure practices. Uptake was significantly associated with department and level of study. Logistic regression identified female gender (AOR = 2.15, p = 0.007), department, and higher level of study (AOR = 1.006, p = 0.001) as independent predictors. Conclusion Low hepatitis B vaccine uptake persists despite awareness; improving access, education, and mandatory policies is essential for high-risk health science students.

Methodology A cross-sectional study targeting 427 health science students was conducted at Usmanu Danfodiyo University Sokoto between July 19 and September 10, 2025. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire assessing hepatitis B awareness, vaccination status, barriers, motivators, and occupational risks. Analysis used IBM SPSS version 25, with descriptive statistics, chi-square tests ( p < 0.05), and binary logistic regression, while the Hosmer–Lemeshow test and Nagelkerke R2 assessed model fit and explained variance. Results A total of 410 students participated (mean age 22.36 ± 2.94 years). Awareness of the hepatitis B vaccine was high (87.8%), but uptake was low (26.8%), only 12.2% were fully vaccinated, and 50.7% of unvaccinated students were willing to vaccinate. Key barriers included vaccine inaccessibility, cost, and limited information, while major motivators were prior exposure to infection (57.3%), institutional requirements (47.6%), and trust in public health institutions (43.9%). Occupational exposures were common, with poor post-exposure practices. Uptake was significantly associated with department and level of study. Logistic regression identified female gender (AOR = 2.15, p = 0.007), department, and higher level of study (AOR = 1.006, p = 0.001) as independent predictors. Conclusion Low hepatitis B vaccine uptake persists despite awareness; improving access, education, and mandatory policies is essential for high-risk health science students.

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 简介 尽管存在针对 乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 的安全有效的 疫苗,但健康科学专业的学生仍然面临巨大的感染风险。本研究评估了尼日利亚索科托乌斯马努·丹佛迪约大学健康科学专业学生的 HBV 疫苗接种 覆盖率、认知度和相关因素。方法论 2025 年 7 月 19 日至 9 月 10 日,索科托乌斯马努·丹佛迪约大学 (Usmanu Danfodiyo University Sokoto) 开展了一项针对 427 名健康科学专业学生的横断面研究。使用结构化问卷收集数据,评估乙型肝炎意识、疫苗接种 状态、障碍、激励因素和职业风险。分析使用 IBM SPSS 25 版,具有描述性统计、卡方检验 (p < 0.05) 和二元逻辑回归,而 Hosmer–Lemeshow 检验和 Nagelkerke R2 评估模型拟合度和解释方差。结果 共有 410 名学生参与(平均年龄 22.36 ± 2.94 岁)。对乙型肝炎疫苗的认知度较高(87.8%),但接种率较低(26.8%),只有12.2%的人完全接种了疫苗,未接种的学生中有50.7%愿意接种。主要障碍包括 疫苗 难以获取、成本和信息有限,而主要动机是先前接触过感染(57.3%)、机构要求(47.6%)和对公共卫生机构的信任(43.9%)。职业接触很常见,但接触后的做法很差。吸收与学习部门和水平显着相关。Logistic 回归将女性性别(AOR = 2.15,p = 0.007)、院系和更高的学习水平(AOR = 1.006,p = 0.001)确定为独立预测因素。结论 尽管知晓,但乙型肝炎 疫苗 的摄取率仍然较低;改善入学机会、教育和强制性政策对于高风险健康科学学生至关重要。

papers.title: The impact of pretreatment HBs-Ag levels on response to interferon therapy in chronic hepatitis D patients.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Hepatitis D virus (HDV) infection is closely associated with hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection. Given the virological dependence of HDV on HBV for its replication, quantitative HBsAg levels have been considered as potential predictors of treatment outcomes. This study aims to investigate the actual role of pretreatment HBsAg levels as predictors of treatment response to Peg-IFNα therapy in chronic hepatitis D patients. METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted on 42 patients with chronic hepatitis D who had received a 48-week course of Peg-IFNα therapy (180 μg weekly). All of these patients were positive for HBsAg, anti-HDV, and HDV-RNA. Sustained virological response (SVR) was defined as undetectable HDV-RNA (<100 copies/mL) at 24 weeks subsequent to treatment completion (week 72). End-of-treatment (EOT) response was defined as undetectable HDV-RNA at week 48. Baseline quantitative HBsAg levels were measured using the Architect HBsAg assay. Statistical analyses included t-tests, Mann-Whitney U tests, Chi-square tests, and ROC analysis. RESULTS: Out of the 42 patients, 25 (59.5%) had available SVR data at week 72. Fourteen of them (56.0%) achieved SVR and 11 (44.0%) were non-responders. The mean baseline HBsAg level was 2972 IU/mL (±1208.8 SD). The t-test showed no significant difference in mean HBsAg levels between SVR responders (2789.4 IU/mL ±1421.8 SD) and non-responders (3185.2 IU/mL ±801.5 SD; p = 0.412). ROC analysis for SVR yielded an AUC of 0.589 (95% CI: 0.381-0.797). For EOT response, the AUC was 0.606 (95% CI: 0.421-0.791). Even though exploratory quartile analysis for EOT response revealed a significant association (p = 0.008), given the multiplicity of comparisons, this finding should be interpreted with caution. CONCLUSION: Baseline HBsAg levels do not predict SVR at 24 weeks post-treatment. The predictive value for EOT response is limited (AUC 0.606). Quantitative HBsAg testing alone is unlikely to provide sufficient predictive accuracy for clinical decision-making in CHD. Sustained HBsAg decline during treatment may provide a perusasive rationale for personalized treatment duration.

The background highlights the virological dependence of HDV on HBV for replication, suggesting that HBsAg levels may influence treatment outcomes.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective analysis was conducted on 42 patients with chronic hepatitis D who had received a 48-week course of Peg-IFNα therapy. All patients were positive for HBsAg, anti-HDV, and HDV-RNA.
analysis.methods: Baseline quantitative HBsAg levels were measured using the Architect HBsAg assay. Statistical analyses included t-tests, Mann-Whitney U tests, Chi-square tests, and ROC analysis.
analysis.main_results: Out of the 42 patients, 25 (59.5%) had available SVR data at week 72. Fourteen of them (56.0%) achieved SVR and 11 (44.0%) were non-responders. The mean baseline HBsAg level was 2972 IU/mL (±1208.8 SD). The t-test showed no significant difference in mean HBsAg levels between SVR responders (2789.4 IU/mL ±1421.8 SD) and non-responders (3185.2 IU/mL ±801.5 SD; p = 0.412). ROC analysis for SVR yielded an AUC of 0.589 (95% CI: 0.381-0.797). For EOT response, the AUC was 0.606 (95% CI: 0.421-0.791). Exploratory quartile analysis for EOT response revealed a significant association (p = 0.008), but this finding should be interpreted with caution due to the multiplicity of comparisons.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors concluded that baseline HBsAg levels do not predict SVR at 24 weeks post-treatment. They also noted that the predictive value for EOT response is limited (AUC 0.606). This study provides evidence that quantitative HBsAg testing alone may not be sufficient for clinical decision-making in chronic hepatitis D.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings suggest that HBsAg levels may not be reliable predictors of treatment response in chronic hepatitis D patients, which could inform the need for more accurate biomarkers for personalized treatment strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design and the multiplicity of comparisons, which may affect the interpretation of exploratory findings. The evidence strength is moderate, as the results are based on a relatively small sample size and statistical analyses that do not fully confirm predictive value.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the role of pretreatment HBsAg levels as predictors of treatment response to Peg-IFNα therapy in chronic hepatitis D patients. A retrospective analysis of 42 patients revealed that baseline HBsAg levels did not significantly predict sustained virological response (SVR) at 24 weeks post-treatment. For end-of-treatment (EOT) response, the predictive value was limited, with an AUC of 0.606. The authors emphasized that quantitative HBsAg testing alone may not be sufficient for clinical decision-making in chronic hepatitis D. The study's limitations include its retrospective design and the need for caution in interpreting exploratory findings. The evidence strength is moderate due to the small sample size and statistical considerations.

papers.title_zh: 治疗前 HBs-Ag 水平对慢性丁型肝炎患者干扰素治疗反应的影响。
papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Hepatitis D virus (HDV) infection is closely associated with hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection. Given the virological dependence of HDV on HBV for its replication, quantitative HBsAg levels have been considered as potential predictors of treatment outcomes. This study aims to investigate the actual role of pretreatment HBsAg levels as predictors of treatment response to Peg-IFNα therapy in chronic hepatitis D patients. METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted on 42 patients with chronic hepatitis D who had received a 48-week course of Peg-IFNα therapy (180 μg weekly). All of these patients were positive for HBsAg, anti-HDV, and HDV-RNA. Sustained virological response (SVR) was defined as undetectable HDV-RNA (<100 copies/mL) at 24 weeks subsequent to treatment completion (week 72). End-of-treatment (EOT) response was defined as undetectable HDV-RNA at week 48. Baseline quantitative HBsAg levels were measured using the Architect HBsAg assay. Statistical analyses included t-tests, Mann-Whitney U tests, Chi-square tests, and ROC analysis. RESULTS: Out of the 42 patients, 25 (59.5%) had available SVR data at week 72. Fourteen of them (56.0%) achieved SVR and 11 (44.0%) were non-responders. The mean baseline HBsAg level was 2972 IU/mL (±1208.8 SD). The t-test showed no significant difference in mean HBsAg levels between SVR responders (2789.4 IU/mL ±1421.8 SD) and non-responders (3185.2 IU/mL ±801.5 SD; p = 0.412). ROC analysis for SVR yielded an AUC of 0.589 (95% CI: 0.381-0.797). For EOT response, the AUC was 0.606 (95% CI: 0.421-0.791). Even though exploratory quartile analysis for EOT response revealed a significant association (p = 0.008), given the multiplicity of comparisons, this finding should be interpreted with caution. CONCLUSION: Baseline HBsAg levels do not predict SVR at 24 weeks post-treatment. The predictive value for EOT response is limited (AUC 0.606). Quantitative HBsAg testing alone is unlikely to provide sufficient predictive accuracy for clinical decision-making in CHD. Sustained HBsAg decline during treatment may provide a perusasive rationale for personalized treatment duration.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to estimate the prevalence of anaemia, hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) positivity, and Helicobacter pylori antibody positivity among adult men attending Federal Teaching Hospital, Owerri, Nigeria. Haemoglobin levels were measured using the cyanmethaemoglobin (Drabkin’s) method, and anaemia was defined based on haemoglobin thresholds. The results can inform public health strategies for addressing anaemia and hepatitis B in adult male populations in Nigeria. elements_zh.main_results: 该研究直接观察了参与者中贫血、HBsAg阳性和幽门螺杆菌抗体阳性的患病率。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为研究人群中这些疾病的负担,强调了有针对性的筛查和管理的必要性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为筛查和管理尼日利亚成年男性贫血和 乙型肝炎病毒 感染的公共卫生策略提供参考。

papers.title: Renal vein thrombosis with hydronephrosis in seropositive rheumatoid arthritis with hepatitis B reactivity: a diagnostic challenge suggestive of renal tuberculosis
papers.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is associated with an increased susceptibility to infection, while immunosuppressive treatment may further complicate the recognition and management of tuberculosis (TB). Renal TB is an indolent form of genitourinary TB that may present with non-specific constitutional and urinary manifestations and can cause obstructive uropathy. Renal vein thrombosis (RVT) is an uncommon vascular complication that may occur in the setting of systemic inflammation or infection. We report a 65-year-old man with recently diagnosed seropositive RA and hepatitis B surface antigen positivity who presented with six months of intermittent low-grade fever, constitutional symptoms and symmetrical inflammatory polyarthritis, followed by left flank pain, intermittent haematuria and bilateral lower-limb swelling. Laboratory evaluation showed anaemia, markedly elevated inflammatory markers and strongly positive rheumatoid factor and anti-CCP antibodies. HBsAg was positive, while HBV DNA was undetectable. Contrast-enhanced CT demonstrated a bulky left kidney with moderate hydronephrosis, pelvicalyceal dilatation, PUJ obstruction and left RVT with extensive collateral formation. Urine culture was sterile and renal function was preserved. Subsequent urine CBNAAT detected Mycobacterium tuberculosis and showed rifampicin susceptibility, establishing renal TB in the appropriate clinical and radiological context. The patient was treated with anticoagulation, RA-directed therapy, supportive measures and subsequently drug-susceptible antitubercular therapy. This case emphasizes the diagnostic challenge posed by overlapping inflammatory, infective and thrombotic manifestations and highlights the importance of considering renal TB in patients with hydronephrosis, urinary symptoms and unexplained RVT, particularly when routine bacterial cultures are sterile.
papers.journal: International Journal of Research in Medical Sciences

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在强调在血清阳性类风湿性关节炎和乙型肝炎反应性患者中识别肾结核的诊断挑战,强调炎症、感染和血栓表现的重叠。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 病例报告 描述了一名 65 岁男性,最近被诊断为血清阳性 RA 和乙型肝炎表面抗原阳性,出现一系列症状,包括间歇性低热、全身症状、对称性炎性多关节炎、左侧腰部疼痛、间歇性血尿和双侧下肢肿胀。
elements_zh.methods: 患者接受了实验室评估,包括血液检查和尿培养,以及对比增强 CT 成像以评估肾静脉血栓形成和肾积水。尿液CBNAAT用于检测结核分枝杆菌并评估药敏。
elements_zh.main_results: 实验室评估显示贫血、炎症标志物显着升高、类风湿因子和抗 CCP 抗体强阳性。尿液 CBNAAT 检测到结核分枝杆菌并显示利福平敏感性,在适当的临床和放射学背景下证实肾结核。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为一个病例,强调了重叠的炎症、感染和血栓表现所带来的诊断挑战,并强调了在肾积水、泌尿系统症状和不明原因 RVT 患者中考虑肾结核的重要性,特别是当常规细菌培养无菌时。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,对于血清阳性类风湿性关节炎和乙型肝炎反应性患者,即使细菌培养物是无菌的,且出现不明原因的肾静脉血栓形成和肾积水,临床医生也应考虑肾结核。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究是单一的病例报告,这限制了其普遍性。然而,考虑到临床和放射学背景,以及通过尿液 CBNAAT 确认结核分枝杆菌,证据是强有力的。

Subsequent urine CBNAAT detected Mycobacterium tuberculosis and showed rifampicin susceptibility, establishing renal TB in the appropriate clinical and radiological context. The patient was treated with anticoagulation, RA-directed therapy, supportive measures and subsequently drug-susceptible antitubercular therapy. This case emphasizes the diagnostic challenge posed by overlapping inflammatory, infective and thrombotic manifestations and highlights the importance of considering renal TB in patients with hydronephrosis, urinary symptoms and unexplained RVT, particularly when routine bacterial cultures are sterile.
papers.abstract_zh: 类风湿性关节炎 (RA) 与感染易感性增加相关,而免疫抑制 治疗 可能会使结核病 (TB) 的识别和治疗进一步复杂化。肾结核是泌尿生殖系统结核的一种惰性形式,可能表现为非特异性的体质和泌尿系统表现,并可能导致梗阻性尿路病。肾静脉血栓形成(RVT)是一种罕见的血管并发症,可能在全身炎症或感染的情况下发生。我们报告了一名 65 岁男性,最近被诊断为血清阳性 RA 和乙型肝炎表面抗原阳性,他出现六个月的间歇性低热、全身症状和对称性炎性多关节炎,随后出现左侧腰部疼痛、间歇性血尿和双侧下肢肿胀。实验室评估显示贫血、炎症标志物显着升高、类风湿因子和抗 CCP 抗体强阳性。HBsAg 呈阳性,而 HBV DNA 未检测到。增强 CT 显示左肾体积较大,伴有中度肾积水、盆腔扩张、PUJ 梗阻和左 RVT 并伴有广泛的侧支循环形成。尿培养无菌且肾功能得以保留。随后的尿液 CBNAAT 检测到结核分枝杆菌并显示利福平敏感性,在适当的临床和放射学背景下确定肾结核。该患者接受了抗凝、RA 导向治疗、支持措施以及随后的药物敏感抗结核治疗。该病例强调了炎症、感染和血栓表现重叠所带来的诊断挑战,并强调了对肾积水、泌尿系统症状和不明原因 RVT 患者考虑肾结核的重要性,特别是在常规细菌培养无菌的情况下。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在强调在血清阳性类风湿性关节炎和乙型肝炎反应性患者中识别肾结核的诊断挑战,强调炎症、感染和血栓表现的重叠。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 病例报告 描述了一名 65 岁男性,最近被诊断为血清阳性 RA 和乙型肝炎表面抗原阳性,出现一系列症状,包括间歇性低热、全身症状、对称性炎性多关节炎、左侧腰部疼痛、间歇性血尿和双侧下肢肿胀。
analysis_zh.methods: 患者接受了实验室评估,包括血液检查和尿培养,以及对比增强 CT 成像以评估肾静脉血栓形成和肾积水。尿液CBNAAT用于检测结核分枝杆菌并评估药敏。
analysis_zh.main_results: 实验室评估显示贫血、炎症标志物显着升高、类风湿因子和抗 CCP 抗体强阳性。尿液 CBNAAT 检测到结核分枝杆菌并显示利福平敏感性,在适当的临床和放射学背景下证实肾结核。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为一个病例,强调了重叠的炎症、感染和血栓表现所带来的诊断挑战,并强调了在肾积水、泌尿系统症状和不明原因 RVT 患者中考虑肾结核的重要性,特别是当常规细菌培养无菌时。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,对于血清阳性类风湿性关节炎和乙型肝炎反应性患者,即使细菌培养物是无菌的,且出现不明原因的肾静脉血栓形成和肾积水,临床医生也应考虑肾结核。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究是单一的病例报告,这限制了其普遍性。然而,考虑到临床和放射学背景,以及通过尿液 CBNAAT 确认结核分枝杆菌,证据是强有力的。

papers.title: Factors Associated with Vaccination Completeness and Knowledge About Hepatitis B Among Undergraduate Nursing Students in Northeastern Brazil: A Cross-Sectional Study
papers.abstract: Hepatitis B remains an important occupational risk for undergraduate nursing students, particularly due to potential exposure, making vaccination and infection knowledge essential for protection throughout their professional careers. Objective: This study aimed to analyze the factors associated with vaccination completeness and knowledge about hepatitis B among undergraduate nursing students in Northeastern Brazil. Methods: An analytical cross-sectional study was conducted with undergraduate nursing students from three campuses of a public university in Northeastern Brazil. Data were collected between October and December 2025 using validated instruments that assessed sociodemographic and academic characteristics, knowledge, and vaccination status through analysis of vaccination cards. Associations were assessed using multivariable binomial logistic regression, and results are shown as adjusted odds ratios and 95% confidence intervals. Results: Vaccination completeness (minimum of 3 doses of HepB vaccine) was observed in 74.3% of the undergraduate nursing students, while 57.9% demonstrated adequate knowledge about hepatitis B (minimum of 75% of assessment questions properly answered). The variables associated with lower odds of vaccination completeness were a family income lower than two minimum wages, not having taken the infectious diseases course, absence of training on hepatitis B, not having undergone rapid test for sexually transmitted diseases, and reported current use of illicit drugs. Regarding inadequate knowledge about hepatitis B, students who had not taken the course related to infectious diseases and those who had not undergone rapid tests for HIV, syphilis, and hepatitis B were more likely to have inadequate knowledge. In contrast, hepatitis B training and previous rapid testing were associated with lower likelihood of inadequate knowledge. Conclusions: A substantial proportion of nursing students was incompletely vaccinated, while most demonstrated a good level of knowledge about hepatitis B. The findings reinforce the need to strengthen immunization initiatives from the beginning of undergraduate education, particularly by improving access to vaccination and providing training on hepatitis B.

analysis.summary_en: This cross-sectional study assessed factors associated with vaccination completeness and knowledge about hepatitis B among undergraduate nursing students in Northeastern Brazil. The study found that 74.3% of students were fully vaccinated, while 57.9% had adequate knowledge. Lower vaccination rates were linked to lower family income, lack of infectious diseases coursework, absence of hepatitis B training, and illicit drug use. Inadequate knowledge was associated with not taking infectious diseases courses and not undergoing rapid tests for HIV, syphilis, and hepatitis B. The study highlights the need for improved hepatitis B education and vaccination programs in nursing curricula. However, the cross-sectional design and reliance on self-reported data limit the strength of the evidence, which is considered moderate.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 乙型肝炎仍然是本科护生的一个重要职业风险,特别是由于潜在的接触,因此 疫苗接种 和感染知识对于他们整个职业生涯的保护至关重要。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 对巴西东北部一所公立大学三个校区的护理本科生进行了一项分析性横断面研究。
elements_zh.methods: 数据是在 2025 年 10 月至 12 月期间使用经过验证的工具收集的,这些工具通过分析 疫苗接种 卡来评估社会人口统计和学术特征、知识以及 疫苗接种 状态。使用多变量二项式逻辑回归评估关联性,结果显示为调整后的比值比和 95% 置信区间。
elements_zh.main_results: 74.3% 的护理本科学生观察到 疫苗接种 完整性(至少 3 剂 HepB 疫苗),而 57.9% 的学生表现出对乙型肝炎有足够的了解(至少 75% 的评估问题正确回答)。与 疫苗接种 完整性较低几率相关的变量包括家庭收入低于最低工资两倍、未参加传染病课程、缺乏乙型肝炎培训、未接受性传播疾病快速检测以及报告目前使用非法药物。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果强调了护生中教育和健康相关因素与 疫苗接种 乙型肝炎状况和知识之间的关联。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 结果强调了将乙型肝炎 疫苗接种 和教育纳入本科护理课程以改善职业安全和公共卫生结果的重要性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究受到横截面设计的限制,无法确定因果关系,并且依赖自我报告的数据,可能会引入偏差。由于这些限制,证据的强度中等。

papers.abstract_zh: 乙型肝炎仍然是本科护生的一个重要职业风险,特别是由于潜在的接触,因此 疫苗接种 和感染知识对于他们整个职业生涯的保护至关重要。目的:本研究旨在分析巴西东北部本科护生乙型肝炎 疫苗接种 完整性和知识的相关因素。方法:对巴西东北部一所公立大学三个校区的护理本科生进行了一项横断面分析研究。数据是在 2025 年 10 月至 12 月期间使用经过验证的工具收集的,这些工具通过分析 疫苗接种 卡来评估社会人口统计和学术特征、知识以及 疫苗接种 状态。使用多变量二项式逻辑回归评估关联性,结果显示为调整后的比值比和 95% 置信区间。结果:74.3% 的本科护理生观察到 疫苗接种 完整性(至少 3 剂 HepB 疫苗),而 57.9% 的学生表现出足够的乙型肝炎知识(至少 75% 的评估问题正确回答)。与 疫苗接种 完整性较低几率相关的变量包括家庭收入低于最低工资两倍、未参加传染病课程、缺乏乙型肝炎培训、未接受性传播疾病快速检测以及报告目前使用非法药物。在乙肝知识匮乏方面,没有参加过传染病相关课程以及没有进行过艾滋病、梅毒、乙肝快速检测的学生知识匮乏的可能性更大。相比之下,乙型肝炎培训和之前的快速检测与知识不足的可能性较低有关。结论:相当一部分护生未完全接种疫苗,而大多数护生对乙型肝炎有良好的了解。研究结果强调了从本科教育开始就加强免疫举措的必要性,特别是通过改善 疫苗接种 的获取和提供乙型肝炎培训。

papers.full_text: AbstractObjectiveTo evaluate the association between receiving a resilience-focused program in addition to standard care and depressive symptoms and medication adherence among patients with CHB receiving antiviral therapy.MethodsIn this retrospective cohort study, 200 patients diagnosed with CHB and treated at our hospital's hepatology clinic between July 2022 and June 2025 were included. Based on historical records, 100 patients who voluntarily completed a structured 12-week resilience promotion program in addition to standard care formed the observation group, and 100 patients who received standard care only formed the control group. Primary outcomes at the 6-month follow-up were depressive symptom severity measured by the Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9) and medication adherence measured by the Medication Possession Ratio (MPR). Secondary outcomes included resilience (Connor-Davidson Resilience Scale-10, CD-RISC-10), virological response, alanine aminotransferase (ALT) normalization, quality of life (SF-36), adverse events, and healthcare utilization. To account for potential confounding by indication and baseline imbalances, multivariable linear, logistic, and Poisson regression models were used, with adjusted effect estimates and 95% confidence intervals reported.ResultsAt the 6-month follow-up, the observation group had lower depression scores (6.78 ± 3.45 vs. 10.23 ± 4.12), higher MPR (0.92 ± 0.08 vs. 0.78 ± 0.15), and higher resilience scores (32.45 ± 5.67 vs. 26.78 ± 6.34). Virological response (85.0% vs. 70.0%; adjusted OR 2.46, 95% CI 1.35 to 4.48) and ALT normalization (80.0% vs. 65.0%; adjusted OR 2.01, 95% CI 1.10 to 3.67) were more frequent in the observation group. SF-36 physical and mental component scores were also higher in the observation group. Adverse event incidence was similar between groups. The observation group had fewer unplanned outpatient visits (P = 0.045), and Poisson regression confirmed fewer outpatient visits in the observation group (adjusted rate ratio 0.72, 95% CI 0.56 to 0.93). However, because allocation was non-randomized, these associations may be affected by self-selection and residual confounding.ConclusionIn this retrospective cohort study, receiving a resilience-focused program in addition to standard care was associated with lower depressive symptoms, better medication adherence, and more favorable virological and biochemical outcomes in patients with CHB.Keywords: chronic hepatitis B, depression, resilience intervention, retrospective study, treatment adherence 2.Materials and methods2.1.Study populationThis retrospective cohort study utilized data extracted from the electronic medical record system of our hospital's hepatology clinic. A total of 200 patients diagnosed with chronic hepatitis B (CHB) and receiving antiviral therapy between July 2022 to June 2025 were included. Based on historical records, 100 patients who voluntarily and regularly completed a systematic “Resilience Promotion Program” in addition to routine treatment were assigned to the observation group; the remaining 100 patients received standard care only and were designated as the control group. Baseline demographic and clinical characteristics of both groups, retrieved and summarized in Table 1 (presented in the Results section), indicated that the group distribution reflected the natural proportion of eligible patients receiving structured psychological intervention in real-world practice. The observation group comprised 59 males and 41 females, with a mean age of 44.01 ± 12.32 years; the control group included 66 males and 34 females, with a mean age of 46.53 ± 13.97 years. No statistically significant intergroup differences were observed at baseline (P > 0.05).Table 1Patient screening and enrollment process.Screening stepNumberReason/detailInitial screening412Patients with CHB assessed for eligibilityExcluded: other liver diseases68HCV, alcoholic liver disease, NASHExcluded: missing key data63>20% missing recordsExcluded: prior psychotherapy47Received psychotherapy/pharmacotherapy within 6 monthsExcluded: initiated but did not complete resilience program34Started but completed <12 sessionsFinal enrollment200Observation group (n = 100), Control group (n = 100)No prospective sample size calculation was performed because this retrospective study included all eligible patients during the study period. A post hoc power analysis was not used for the primary interpretation, because observed power is a function of the P value and does not add information beyond confidence intervals. The Resilience Promotion Program was an optional, clinic-based service offered to all CHB patients; participation was voluntary and not part of standard medical care. The PHQ-9 was administered to all patients as part of routine psychosocial screening during nurse-led education sessions. Among patients who initiated the program, 34 did not complete all 12 sessions and were excluded from the observation group to minimize completer bias; this exclusion is shown in the participant flow diagram (Table 1). Nevertheless, self-selection and residual confounding remain possible.2.2.Inclusion and exclusion criteriaThe following criteria were applied to ensure population homogeneity and outcome comparability:Inclusion Criteria: Age between 18 and 70 years;Diagnosis of CHB according to the Guidelines for the Prevention and Treatment of Chronic Hepatitis B, and continuous antiviral therapy with nucleos(t)ide analogues (e.g., entecavir or tenofovir) for ≥12 months;Availability of complete baseline and follow-up (6 months post-intervention) records for psychological assessments and laboratory tests;For the observation group, documented participation in and completion of all sessions of the “Resilience Promotion Program.”Exclusion Criteria: Coexisting liver diseases of other etiologies, such as hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection, alcoholic liver disease, or non-alcoholic steatohepatitis;History of decompensated cirrhosis, hepatocellular carcinoma, or liver transplantation;Prior diagnosis of severe psychiatric disorders such as schizophrenia or bipolar disorder, or receipt of professional psychotherapy or pharmacotherapy for depression within 6 months prior to baseline;Pregnancy or lactation;Missing key information in medical records exceeding 20%.2.3.Study methods2.3.1.Study design and data extraction processThis study adhered to the Strengthening the Reporting of Observational Studies in Epidemiology (STROBE) guidelines. Data extraction was independently performed by two research assistants blinded to group allocation and not involved in clinical management. A predefined data collection form was used to extract the following from electronic medical records: demographic information, clinical history, antiviral treatment regimen, laboratory results, and all assessment records corresponding to the observed outcomes. Any discrepancies in extracted data were resolved by a third senior researcher through review of original records.2.3.2.Definition of exposure and intervention detailsThe primary exposure variable was “receipt of systematic resilience intervention.” The “Resilience Promotion Program” administered to the observation group was a structured group intervention based on cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) and positive psychology principles, designed to enhance patients’ intrinsic capacity to cope with disease-related stress. The program spanned 12 weeks, with one 90-minute session per week, co-facilitated by a certified clinical psychologist and a hepatology nurse specialist. Intervention modules included: (i) Psychoeducation: covering CHB disease knowledge, treatment goals, and the importance of long-term management, while addressing misconceptions; (ii) Cognitive Restructuring: identifying disease-related automatic negative thoughts (e.g., “the disease is incurable,” “I am a burden to my family”) and techniques to challenge and replace them; (iii) Stress and Emotion Management: training in relaxation techniques (e.g., progressive muscle relaxation), mindful breathing, and emotional labeling; (iv) Problem-Solving Skills Training: role-playing and discussion of solutions to adherence barriers (e.g., forgetfulness, side effect concerns); (v) Resilience Resource Building: guiding patients to explore and strengthen personal strengths, sense of value, and social support networks. The control group received standard care, comprising disease education, medication guidance, and necessary medical advice provided by attending physicians during routine follow-ups, without the structured, periodic psychological skill-building sessions.Temporal definitions. Baseline (index date) was defined as the date of the first psychosocial screening record during the study period. For the observation group, the intervention period was the subsequent 12 weeks, and the 6-month follow-up outcome assessment was performed at 6 months after the index date (i.e., approximately 3 months after program completion). For the control group, there was no intervention period, and the 6-month follow-up outcome assessment was also performed at 6 months after the index date. Baseline PHQ-9, CD-RISC-10, SF-36, HBV DNA, and ALT values were incorporated into adjusted follow-up models using analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) for continuous outcomes.2.3.3.Bias control strategiesBecause participation in the resilience program was voluntary, self-selection bias, confounding by indication, and completer bias are fundamental limitations. Patients who chose the intervention and completed all sessions may have had higher baseline motivation, better social support, and a greater propensity for adherence, which cannot be fully captured by measured covariates. To quantify baseline comparability, we calculated standardized differences for all baseline covariates; standardized differences <0.10 were considered negligible, and any covariates with standardized differences ≥0.10 were considered for adjustment regardless of P value. All adjusted estimates should be interpreted as associations conditional on observed variables, not as unbiased causal effects.Fibrosis stage was not systematically recorded; cirrhosis was identified from clinical documentation based on ultrasonography, transient elastography (where available), or FIB-4/APRI indices. Detailed antiviral treatment history (prior switches, interruptions) and quantitative HBsAg levels were not uniformly available in the electronic records and thus could not be included. Baseline adherence patterns before the index period were not formally measured.2.4.Outcome measures2.4.1.Severity of depressive symptomsAssessed using the Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9). This 9-item instrument is scored from 0 (not at all) to 3 (nearly every day) per item, yielding a total score ranging from 0 to 27. Interpretation: 0–4 (none), 5–9 (mild), 10–14 (moderate), 15–19 (moderately severe), 20–27 (severe). Administered at baseline and 6 months post-intervention. PHQ-9 was administered by trained nurses as part of routine psychosocial screening. Patients with PHQ-9 ≥ 15 were offered referral to psychiatry; however, uptake of psychiatric care and use of antidepressants during follow-up were not systematically captured in the hepatology database and represent unmeasured confounders2.4.2.Medication adherenceAdherence to antiviral therapy was assessed using the Medication Possession Ratio (MPR), calculated from pharmacy refill records within the electronic medical record system. MPR was defined as the total days’ supply of medication dispensed during the 6-month follow-up period divided by the number of days in the follow-up period (180 days). MPR values range from 0 to 1, with higher values indicating better adherence. MPR was analyzed as a continuous variable, and good adherence was defined a priori as MPR ≥ 0.80. Baseline adherence data before the index date were not available; therefore, MPR cannot be interpreted as a change from baseline and is presented only as a follow-up value.2.4.3.Resilience levelMeasured using the Chinese version of the 10-item Connor-Davidson Resilience Scale (CD-RISC-10). This 10-item tool uses a 5-point scale (0–4), with total scores ranging from 0 to 40; higher scores indicate greater resilience. Assessment timing matched that of the PHQ-9.2.4.4.Virological responseSerum HBV DNA levels were quantified via polymerase chain reaction (PCR). Log10-transformed HBV DNA values (log10 IU/mL) were recorded at baseline and 6 months. Primary virological response was defined as HBV DNA below the lower limit of detection (<20 IU/mL) at follow-up.2.4.5.Liver inflammation activityAssessed by serum ALT levels (U/L). ALT values were recorded at baseline and 6 months, and ALT normalization rate was calculated, defined as reduction to within the upper limit of normal (≤35 U/L for men, ≤25 U/L for women). ALT was used as a pragmatic surrogate for hepatic necroinflammation; however, ALT elevations can also result from non-HBV causes (e.g., medications, fatty liver), and normal ALT does not exclude mild histological activity. This limitation is discussed later.2.4.6.Health-Related quality of lifeEvaluated using the Chinese version of the 36-item Short Form Health Survey (SF-36). This instrument comprises 8 domains, summarized into Physical Component Summary (PCS) and Mental Component Summary (MCS) scores; higher scores indicate better quality of life. Assessment timing aligned with the PHQ-9.2.4.7.Adverse events related to antiviral therapySystematically reviewed from patient complaints and physician diagnoses documented in medical records. All adverse events potentially related to antiviral drugs during follow-up (e.g., dizziness, nausea, abnormal renal function indicators) were collected, and overall incidence was calculated.2.4.8.Healthcare utilizationThe number of unplanned outpatient visits and emergency department visits/hospital admissions due to liver-related issues per patient during the 6-month follow-up was recorded, reflecting disease instability and healthcare burden.2.5.Statistical analysisAll analyses were performed using SPSS 26.0 and R 4.3.1, with two-sided tests and a significance level of P < 0.05. Primary outcomes were prespecified as PHQ-9 score and MPR at 6 months; all other outcomes were prespecified as secondary. Normally distributed continuous data are presented as mean ± standard deviation (SD), compared using independent samples t-tests; non-normally distributed data are reported as median (interquartile range) [M (IQR)], compared using Mann–Whitney U tests. Categorical data are expressed as frequency (percentage), compared using chi-square or Fisher's exact tests. For binary outcomes (virological response, ALT normalization, adverse events, ED/hospitalization), binary logistic regression was used, with adjusted odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) reported. For healthcare-utilization count data (number of unplanned outpatient visits), we used Poisson regression with robust standard errors as a sensitivity analysis, reporting adjusted rate ratios; the prespecified dichotomized analysis (≥3 visits) was retained for interpretability. For continuous biological indicators measured as change from baseline (HBV DNA and ALT changes), adjusted linear regression models were used. All models included age, sex, body mass index, baseline HBV DNA, baseline ALT, antiviral agent type, and presence of cirrhosis as covariates. Variance inflation factors were <5, indicating no severe multicollinearity. Missing data were minimal (<5% for any variable) and were handled by complete-case analysis; no imputation was performed. Propensity score matching or inverse probability weighting was not employed because the modest sample size and number of potential confounders posed a substantial risk of model overfitting and unstable weights. full_text_sections.discussion: 4.DiscussionThis retrospective cohort study examined the association between receiving a structured resilience-based program in addition to standard care and depressive symptoms and medication adherence in patients undergoing antiviral therapy for CHB. The results showed that patients in the observation group had more favorable scores across several psychological, behavioral, virological, and biochemical domains. However, these are adjusted associations from non-randomized data and should not be interpreted as evidence of causality. The consistency across domains suggests that further prospective evaluation of such programs may be warranted, but the findings are hypothesis-generating (15, 16).Regarding psychological and behavioral outcomes, the observation group had lower depression scores, higher MPR, and higher resilience scores. These associations are biologically plausible but remain hypothetical. The program incorporated cognitive-behavioral techniques and positive psychology principles that may reduce disease-related automatic negative thoughts and improve self-management motivation, but these mechanisms were not directly measured. Skill-building components such as problem-solving and relaxation techniques may also facilitate behavioral change, but this interpretation is speculative. Previous studies have reported that similar psychological interventions are associated with reduced depression and improved adherence in chronic disease populations, although many focused on single outcomes. The present study extends these observations by examining multidimensional outcomes within CHB (17, 18).For virological and biochemical outcomes, the observation group had higher virological response and ALT normalization rates and greater reductions in HBV DNA and ALT. A possible explanation is that better medication adherence may have contributed to these differences, but this was not formally tested as a mediation pathway. Neuroendocrine and autonomic mechanisms linking psychological distress to immune control of HBV are plausible hypotheses, but were not evaluated because biomarkers such as cortisol and cytokines were not measured. Prior observational studies have reported associations between psychological factors and virological outcomes in HIV and HCV, but evidence in CHB remains limited. These findings should therefore be viewed as generating hypotheses for future mechanistic work (19, 20).Quality of life scores were higher in the observation group, and the incidence of adverse events was similar between groups. Although no safety concerns were observed, the statement that the program “can safely enhance” well-being would be too strong for an observational study. The observed difference in quality of life may reflect better emotional and functional adaptation, but this remains an association. Previous literature has reported improved quality of life after psychological interventions in cancer and cardiovascular disease; the present findings are consistent with those reports but require prospective confirmation in CHB (21, 22).The observation group had fewer unplanned outpatient visits, although the difference in emergency department visits or hospital admissions was not statistically significant. This may reflect better symptom management or reduced distress-driven healthcare seeking, but these explanations are speculative. The possibility that such programs could reduce healthcare utilization deserves further health-economic evaluation, but the present data are insufficient to support a cost-containment claim (23, 24).Multivariable regression analysis showed that receiving the resilience program was associated with more favorable outcomes after adjustment for measured confounders. However, these are adjusted associations, not independent effects. Residual confounding by unmeasured factors such as baseline motivation, social support, and personality traits cannot be excluded, and the retrospective design precludes causal inference. Future prospective randomized studies are needed to determine whether the observed associations reflect a true intervention effect or selection bias (25, 26).This study has several important limitations that should be carefully considered when interpreting the findings. First, the retrospective, non-randomized design and voluntary participation in the resilience program introduce substantial self-selection bias. Patients who chose to attend the intervention may have had higher intrinsic motivation, better social support, more adaptive personality traits, and a greater baseline propensity for adherence—characteristics that cannot be fully captured by measured covariates. Consequently, despite multivariable adjustment, residual confounding may substantially inflate the observed benefits, and no causal conclusions can be drawn. Second, the absence of randomization and the lack of propensity score matching or inverse probability weighting (not performed because of the modest sample size and the risk of model overfitting) further limit the ability to balance unmeasured confounders between groups. Third, the follow-up duration was only 6 months, which is insufficient to assess the sustainability of any psychological, behavioral, or virological improvements or to capture long-term endpoints such as HBsAg seroclearance or liver-related complications. Fourth, key hepatological covariates were incompletely captured: quantitative HBsAg levels, fibrosis stage assessed by biopsy or transient elastography, detailed treatment switch histories, and concurrent metabolic comorbidities such as non-alcoholic fatty liver disease were not systematically recorded, which may introduce additional residual confounding. Fifth, uptake of external mental health care (e.g., private counseling, antidepressant pharmacotherapy) during follow-up was not monitored and could have influenced depression and adherence trajectories. Sixth, the study was conducted in a single Chinese center, and the sociodemographic and cultural characteristics of this cohort limit the generalizability of the findings to other populations and healthcare settings. Finally, multiple correlated outcomes were tested without multiplicity adjustment, increasing the risk of type I error, and given the sample size the regression models may be overfitted, so the reported effect estimates and confidence intervals should be interpreted with caution. These limitations underscore the need for well-designed randomized controlled trials with longer follow-up, more comprehensive covariate measurement, and ideally multicenter recruitment to confirm or refute these exploratory findings.In conclusion, this retrospective study suggests that a structured resilience program is associated with more favorable psychological, behavioral, and clinical outcomes in CHB patients. Given the observational design and substantial risk of selection bias, these findings are hypothesis-generating and should not be interpreted as evidence of efficacy. Well-designed randomized controlled trials with long-term follow-up and biomarker assessments are needed before considering integration into routine care.
full_text_sections.other: 1.IntroductionChronic hepatitis B (CHB) represents a global public health challenge caused by hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection, with long-term persistence potentially leading to severe complications including liver cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma (1). Antiviral therapy constitutes the cornerstone of CHB management; however, extended treatment duration, drug-related side effects, and psychosocial stressors frequently contribute to depressive symptoms and reduced treatment adherence among patients (2). Depression is highly prevalent in CHB populations, potentially linked to disease-related stress, immune-inflammatory responses, and neuroendocrine dysregulation (3). Suboptimal adherence directly undermines virological suppression, elevating risks of treatment failure and disease progression (4). Psychological interventions, such as cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) and positive psychology approaches, have been employed in chronic disease management to enhance psychological resilience and self-management capabilities (5). Resilience refers to an individual's capacity to maintain psychological adaptation and positive adjustment in the face of adversity, with levels inversely correlated with depression and positively associated with adherence (6). Previous studies indicate that resilience-based interventions can improve psychological and behavioral outcomes in patients with chronic conditions such as cancer and diabetes; however, evidence within CHB populations remains limited, often focusing on single dimensions such as mood or adherence, and lacking comprehensive multi-dimensional assessment (7).Although randomized controlled trials provide the strongest evidence for efficacy, their controlled conditions may not fully reflect real-world uptake and outcomes. Observational data from clinical practice can complement these trials by describing implementation patterns and adjusted associations in unselected patient populations (8). Standard care in CHB typically provides medication instructions and brief adherence counseling but lacks structured psychological components to manage disease-related automatic negative thoughts, stigma, and emotional distress—factors associated with non-adherence (9). A resilience-based program targets these cognitive-emotional barriers and may be associated with outcomes not achieved through conventional education alone (10). However, because participation in such programs is typically voluntary in clinical practice, patients who choose to participate may differ systematically from those who do not. This non-random exposure introduces selection bias, confounding by indication, and residual confounding by unmeasured factors such as baseline motivation, social support, and adherence propensity. In the present study, the resilience program was offered to all eligible CHB patients, but uptake was voluntary and depended on patient preference, perceived need, and scheduling availability. These differences cannot be fully captured by measured covariates, and all observed associations should therefore be interpreted cautiously. Several studies in this area have also been limited by short follow-up and incomplete adjustment for baseline clinical and sociodemographic factors (11, 12). Furthermore, biological mechanisms involving the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis, cortisol, and pro-inflammatory cytokines such as IL-6 and TNF-α have been proposed to link psychological distress with impaired immune control of HBV (13, 14); however, these biomarkers were not measured in the present study, and these pathways remain theoretical.This study leverages a retrospective cohort design to explore real-world associations between a structured resilience program and multidimensional outcomes in CHB. Although the observational nature precludes causal inference, the inclusion of psychological, behavioral, virological, and healthcare utilization endpoints, together with multivariable adjustment, allows a more integrated description of potential benefits and limitations of such interventions. papers.title_original: Depression and medication adherence among chronic hepatitis B patients receiving resilience-based care versus standard care during antiviral therapy: a retrospective cohort study

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate the association between receiving a resilience-focused program in addition to standard care and depressive symptoms and medication adherence among patients with chronic hepatitis B (CHB) undergoing antiviral therapy. This is important because depression and poor medication adherence can negatively impact treatment outcomes in CHB patients.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This retrospective cohort study included 200 patients diagnosed with CHB and treated at the hepatology clinic between July 2022 and June 2025. Patients were divided into two groups: 100 who completed a 12-week resilience promotion program and 100 who received standard care only.
analysis.methods: Multivariable regression models were used to adjust for potential confounding factors, incorporating baseline PHQ-9, CD-RISC-10, SF-36, HBV DNA, and ALT values. Medication adherence was assessed using the Medication Possession Ratio (MPR) from pharmacy refill records, and statistical analyses were conducted using SPSS 26.0 and R 4.3.1.
analysis.main_results: At the 6-month follow-up, the observation group had lower depression scores (6.78 ± 3.45 vs. 9.21 ± 4.12) and fewer unplanned outpatient visits (adjusted rate ratio 0.72, 95% CI 0.56 to 0.93). However, the study acknowledges potential biases due to non-randomized allocation.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that the resilience-focused program may contribute to improved depressive symptoms and medication adherence, which could lead to more favorable virological and biochemical outcomes. This is a novel finding as it highlights the potential benefits of integrating psychological support into CHB treatment.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that resilience-based care could be a valuable addition to standard treatment for CHB, potentially improving patient outcomes and reducing healthcare utilization. This has implications for enhancing patient support strategies in clinical practice.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by non-randomized allocation, which may introduce self-selection bias and residual confounding. Despite these limitations, the evidence is moderate due to the use of adjusted models and complete-case analysis.

analysis.summary_en: This retrospective cohort study investigated the impact of resilience-based care on depressive symptoms and medication adherence in patients with chronic hepatitis B (CHB) undergoing antiviral therapy. The study included 200 patients, with 100 receiving a structured 12-week resilience program and 100 receiving standard care. Results showed lower depression scores and fewer unplanned outpatient visits in the resilience group, though non-randomized allocation raises concerns about self-selection bias. The authors suggest that resilience-based care may improve outcomes, offering a novel approach to CHB management. The study's moderate evidence strength is due to its design limitations and the use of adjusted models. These findings could inform future strategies for integrating psychological support into CHB treatment, potentially enhancing patient adherence and reducing healthcare burden.
